lines.text: Dead March. Enter the funeral of King Henry the Fifth, attended on by the Duke of Bedford, Regent of France; the Duke of Gloucester, Protector; the Duke of Exeter, the Earl of Warwick, the Bishop of Winchester, the Duke of Somerset with Heralds, &c.

lines.speaker: BEDFORD
lines.text: Hung be the heavens with black, yield day to night!

lines.speaker: BEDFORD
lines.text: Comets, importing change of times and states,

lines.speaker: BEDFORD
lines.text: Brandish your crystal tresses in the sky,

lines.speaker: BEDFORD
lines.text: And with them scourge the bad revolting stars

lines.speaker: BEDFORD
lines.text: That have consented unto Henry’s death:

lines.speaker: BEDFORD
lines.text: King Henry the Fifth, too famous to live long!

lines.speaker: BEDFORD
lines.text: England ne’er lost a king of so much worth.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: England ne’er had a king until his time.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Virtue he had, deserving to command;

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: His brandish’d sword did blind men with his beams;

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: His arms spread wider than a dragon’s wings;

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: His sparkling eyes, replete with wrathful fire,

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: More dazzled and drove back his enemies

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Than mid-day sun fierce bent against their faces.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: What should I say? His deeds exceed all speech.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: He ne’er lift up his hand but conquered.

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: We mourn in black; why mourn we not in blood?

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: Henry is dead and never shall revive.

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: Upon a wooden coffin we attend,

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: And Death’s dishonourable victory

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: We with our stately presence glorify,

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: Like captives bound to a triumphant car.

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: What! Shall we curse the planets of mishap

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: That plotted thus our glory’s overthrow?

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: Or shall we think the subtle-witted French

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: Conjurers and sorcerers, that, afraid of him,

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: By magic verses have contriv’d his end?

lines.speaker: WINCHESTER
lines.text: He was a king bless’d of the King of kings;

lines.speaker: WINCHESTER
lines.text: Unto the French the dreadful judgement-day

lines.speaker: WINCHESTER
lines.text: So dreadful will not be as was his sight.

lines.speaker: WINCHESTER
lines.text: The battles of the Lord of Hosts he fought:

lines.speaker: WINCHESTER
lines.text: The Church’s prayers made him so prosperous.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: The Church! Where is it? Had not churchmen pray’d,

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: His thread of life had not so soon decay’d.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: None do you like but an effeminate prince,

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Whom like a school-boy you may overawe.

lines.speaker: WINCHESTER
lines.text: Gloucester, whate’er we like, thou art Protector,

lines.speaker: WINCHESTER
lines.text: And lookest to command the Prince and realm.

lines.speaker: WINCHESTER
lines.text: Thy wife is proud; she holdeth thee in awe

lines.speaker: WINCHESTER
lines.text: More than God or religious churchmen may.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Name not religion, for thou lov’st the flesh,

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: And ne’er throughout the year to church thou go’st,

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Except it be to pray against thy foes.

lines.speaker: BEDFORD
lines.text: Cease, cease these jars, and rest your minds in peace;

lines.speaker: BEDFORD
lines.text: Let’s to the altar; heralds, wait on us.

lines.speaker: BEDFORD
lines.text: Instead of gold, we’ll offer up our arms,

lines.speaker: BEDFORD
lines.text: Since arms avail not, now that Henry’s dead.

lines.speaker: BEDFORD
lines.text: Posterity, await for wretched years,

lines.speaker: BEDFORD
lines.text: When at their mothers’ moist eyes babes shall suck,

lines.speaker: BEDFORD
lines.text: Our isle be made a nourish of salt tears,

lines.speaker: BEDFORD
lines.text: And none but women left to wail the dead.

lines.speaker: BEDFORD
lines.text: Henry the Fifth, thy ghost I invocate:

lines.speaker: BEDFORD
lines.text: Prosper this realm, keep it from civil broils,

lines.speaker: BEDFORD
lines.text: Combat with adverse planets in the heavens.

lines.speaker: BEDFORD
lines.text: A far more glorious star thy soul will make

lines.speaker: BEDFORD
lines.text: Than Julius Caesar or bright—
Enter a Messenger.

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: My honourable lords, health to you all!

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: Sad tidings bring I to you out of France,

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: Of loss, of slaughter, and discomfiture:

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: Guienne, Champaigne, Rheims, Rouen, Orleans,

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: Paris, Guysors, Poictiers, are all quite lost.

lines.speaker: BEDFORD
lines.text: What say’st thou, man, before dead Henry’s corse?

lines.speaker: BEDFORD
lines.text: Speak softly, or the loss of those great towns

lines.speaker: BEDFORD
lines.text: Will make him burst his lead and rise from death.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Is Paris lost? Is Rouen yielded up?

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: If Henry were recall’d to life again,

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: These news would cause him once more yield the ghost.

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: How were they lost? What treachery was us’d?

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: No treachery, but want of men and money.

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: Amongst the soldiers this is muttered:

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: That here you maintain several factions

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: And whilst a field should be dispatch’d and fought,

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: You are disputing of your generals.

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: One would have lingering wars with little cost;

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: Another would fly swift, but wanteth wings;

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: A third thinks, without expense at all,

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: By guileful fair words peace may be obtain’d.

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: Awake, awake, English nobility!

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: Let not sloth dim your honours new-begot.

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: Cropp’d are the flower-de-luces in your arms;

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: Of England’s coat one half is cut away.
[_He exits._]

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: Were our tears wanting to this funeral,

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: These tidings would call forth their flowing tides.

lines.speaker: BEDFORD
lines.text: Me they concern; Regent I am of France.

lines.speaker: BEDFORD
lines.text: Give me my steeled coat. I’ll fight for France.

lines.speaker: BEDFORD
lines.text: Away with these disgraceful wailing robes!

lines.speaker: BEDFORD
lines.text: Wounds will I lend the French instead of eyes,

lines.speaker: BEDFORD
lines.text: To weep their intermissive miseries.
Enter to them another Messenger.

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: Lords, view these letters full of bad mischance.

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: France is revolted from the English quite,

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: Except some petty towns of no import.

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: The Dauphin Charles is crowned king in Rheims;

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: The Bastard of Orleans with him is join’d;

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: Reignier, Duke of Anjou, doth take his part;

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: The Duke of Alençon flieth to his side.
[_He exits._]

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: The Dauphin crowned king! All fly to him!

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: O, whither shall we fly from this reproach?

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: We will not fly but to our enemies’ throats.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Bedford, if thou be slack, I’ll fight it out.

lines.speaker: BEDFORD
lines.text: Gloucester, why doubt’st thou of my forwardness?

lines.speaker: BEDFORD
lines.text: An army have I muster’d in my thoughts,

lines.speaker: BEDFORD
lines.text: Wherewith already France is overrun.
Enter another Messenger.

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: My gracious lords, to add to your laments,

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: Wherewith you now bedew King Henry’s hearse,

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: I must inform you of a dismal fight

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: Betwixt the stout Lord Talbot and the French.

lines.speaker: WINCHESTER
lines.text: What! Wherein Talbot overcame, is’t so?

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: O no, wherein Lord Talbot was o’erthrown.

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: The circumstance I’ll tell you more at large.

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: The tenth of August last this dreadful lord,

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: Retiring from the siege of Orleans,

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: Having full scarce six thousand in his troop,

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: By three and twenty thousand of the French

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: Was round encompassed and set upon.

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: No leisure had he to enrank his men;

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: He wanted pikes to set before his archers;

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: Instead whereof sharp stakes pluck’d out of hedges

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: They pitched in the ground confusedly

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: To keep the horsemen off from breaking in.

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: More than three hours the fight continued;

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: Where valiant Talbot, above human thought,

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: Enacted wonders with his sword and lance.

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: Hundreds he sent to hell, and none durst stand him;

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: Here, there, and everywhere, enrag’d he slew.

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: The French exclaim’d the devil was in arms;

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: All the whole army stood agaz’d on him.

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: His soldiers, spying his undaunted spirit,

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: “A Talbot! a Talbot!” cried out amain,

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: And rush’d into the bowels of the battle.

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: Here had the conquest fully been seal’d up

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: If Sir John Fastolf had not play’d the coward.

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: He, being in the vaward, plac’d behind

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: With purpose to relieve and follow them,

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: Cowardly fled, not having struck one stroke.

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: Hence grew the general wrack and massacre.

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: Enclosed were they with their enemies.

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: A base Walloon, to win the Dauphin’s grace,

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: Thrust Talbot with a spear into the back,

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: Whom all France, with their chief assembled strength,

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: Durst not presume to look once in the face.

lines.speaker: BEDFORD
lines.text: Is Talbot slain? Then I will slay myself,

lines.speaker: BEDFORD
lines.text: For living idly here, in pomp and ease,

lines.speaker: BEDFORD
lines.text: Whilst such a worthy leader, wanting aid,

lines.speaker: BEDFORD
lines.text: Unto his dastard foemen is betray’d.

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: O no, he lives, but is took prisoner,

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: And Lord Scales with him, and Lord Hungerford;

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: Most of the rest slaughter’d or took likewise.

lines.speaker: BEDFORD
lines.text: His ransom there is none but I shall pay.

lines.speaker: BEDFORD
lines.text: I’ll hale the Dauphin headlong from his throne;

lines.speaker: BEDFORD
lines.text: His crown shall be the ransom of my friend;

lines.speaker: BEDFORD
lines.text: Four of their lords I’ll change for one of ours.

lines.speaker: BEDFORD
lines.text: Farewell, my masters; to my task will I;

lines.speaker: BEDFORD
lines.text: Bonfires in France forthwith I am to make

lines.speaker: BEDFORD
lines.text: To keep our great Saint George’s feast withal.

lines.speaker: BEDFORD
lines.text: Ten thousand soldiers with me I will take,

lines.speaker: BEDFORD
lines.text: Whose bloody deeds shall make all Europe quake.

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: So you had need; for Orleans is besieg’d

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: The English army is grown weak and faint;

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: The Earl of Salisbury craveth supply

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: And hardly keeps his men from mutiny,

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: Since they, so few, watch such a multitude.
[_He exits._]

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: Remember, lords, your oaths to Henry sworn,

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: Either to quell the Dauphin utterly,

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: Or bring him in obedience to your yoke.

lines.speaker: BEDFORD
lines.text: I do remember it, and here take my leave

lines.speaker: BEDFORD
lines.text: To go about my preparation.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: I’ll to the Tower with all the haste I can

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: To view th’ artillery and munition;

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: And then I will proclaim young Henry king.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: To Eltham will I, where the young King is,

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: Being ordain’d his special governor;

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: And for his safety there I’ll best devise.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: WINCHESTER
lines.text: Each hath his place and function to attend.

lines.speaker: WINCHESTER
lines.text: I am left out; for me nothing remains.

lines.speaker: WINCHESTER
lines.text: But long I will not be Jack out of office.

lines.speaker: WINCHESTER
lines.text: The King from Eltham I intend to steal,

lines.speaker: WINCHESTER
lines.text: And sit at chiefest stern of public weal.
[_Exeunt._]
Sound a Flourish. Enter  Charles, Alençon and Reignier, marching with Drum and Soldiers.

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: Mars his true moving, even as in the heavens

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: So in the earth, to this day is not known.

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: Late did he shine upon the English side;

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: Now we are victors; upon us he smiles.

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: What towns of any moment but we have?

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: At pleasure here we lie near Orleans,

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: Otherwhiles the famish’d English, like pale ghosts,

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: Faintly besiege us one hour in a month.

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: ALENÇON.

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: They want their porridge and their fat bull beeves.

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: Either they must be dieted like mules

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: And have their provender tied to their mouths,

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: Or piteous they will look, like drowned mice.

lines.speaker: REIGNIER
lines.text: Let’s raise the siege. Why live we idly here?

lines.speaker: REIGNIER
lines.text: Talbot is taken, whom we wont to fear.

lines.speaker: REIGNIER
lines.text: Remaineth none but mad-brain’d Salisbury,

lines.speaker: REIGNIER
lines.text: And he may well in fretting spend his gall;

lines.speaker: REIGNIER
lines.text: Nor men nor money hath he to make war.

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: Sound, sound alarum! We will rush on them.

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: Now for the honour of the forlorn French!

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: Him I forgive my death that killeth me

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: When he sees me go back one foot or fly.
[_Exeunt._]

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: Here alarum; they are beaten back by the English, with great loss.
Re-enter Charles, Alençon and Reignier.

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: Who ever saw the like? What men have I!

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: Dogs, cowards, dastards! I would ne’er have fled

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: But that they left me ’midst my enemies.

lines.speaker: REIGNIER
lines.text: Salisbury is a desperate homicide;

lines.speaker: REIGNIER
lines.text: He fighteth as one weary of his life.

lines.speaker: REIGNIER
lines.text: The other lords, like lions wanting food,

lines.speaker: REIGNIER
lines.text: Do rush upon us as their hungry prey.

lines.speaker: REIGNIER
lines.text: ALENÇON.

lines.speaker: REIGNIER
lines.text: Froissart, a countryman of ours, records,

lines.speaker: REIGNIER
lines.text: England all Olivers and Rowlands bred

lines.speaker: REIGNIER
lines.text: During the time Edward the Third did reign.

lines.speaker: REIGNIER
lines.text: More truly now may this be verified;

lines.speaker: REIGNIER
lines.text: For none but Samsons and Goliases

lines.speaker: REIGNIER
lines.text: It sendeth forth to skirmish. One to ten!

lines.speaker: REIGNIER
lines.text: Lean raw-bon’d rascals! Who would e’er suppose

lines.speaker: REIGNIER
lines.text: They had such courage and audacity?

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: Let’s leave this town; for they are hare-brain’d slaves,

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: And hunger will enforce them to be more eager.

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: Of old I know them; rather with their teeth

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: The walls they’ll tear down than forsake the siege.

lines.speaker: REIGNIER
lines.text: I think by some odd gimmers or device

lines.speaker: REIGNIER
lines.text: Their arms are set like clocks, still to strike on;

lines.speaker: REIGNIER
lines.text: Else ne’er could they hold out so as they do.

lines.speaker: REIGNIER
lines.text: By my consent, we’ll even let them alone.

lines.speaker: REIGNIER
lines.text: ALENÇON.

lines.speaker: REIGNIER
lines.text: Be it so.
Enter the Bastard of Orleans.

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: Where’s the Prince Dauphin? I have news for him.

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: Bastard of Orleans, thrice welcome to us.

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: Methinks your looks are sad, your cheer appall’d.

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: Hath the late overthrow wrought this offence?

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: Be not dismay’d, for succour is at hand.

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: A holy maid hither with me I bring,

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: Which, by a vision sent to her from heaven

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: Ordained is to raise this tedious siege

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: And drive the English forth the bounds of France.

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: The spirit of deep prophecy she hath,

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: Exceeding the nine sibyls of old Rome.

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: What’s past and what’s to come she can descry.

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: Speak, shall I call her in? Believe my words,

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: For they are certain and unfallible.

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: Go, call her in.
[_Exit Bastard._]

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: But first, to try her skill,

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: Reignier, stand thou as Dauphin in my place;

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: Question her proudly; let thy looks be stern.

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: By this means shall we sound what skill she hath.
Re-enter the Bastard of Orleans, with Joan la Pucelle.

lines.speaker: REIGNIER
lines.text: Fair maid, is ’t thou wilt do these wondrous feats?

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: Reignier is ’t thou that thinkest to beguile me?

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: Where is the Dauphin? Come, come from behind;

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: I know thee well, though never seen before.

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: Be not amazed, there’s nothing hid from me.

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: In private will I talk with thee apart.

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: Stand back, you lords, and give us leave awhile.

lines.speaker: REIGNIER
lines.text: She takes upon her bravely at first dash.

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: Dauphin, I am by birth a shepherd’s daughter,

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: My wit untrain’d in any kind of art.

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: Heaven and our Lady gracious hath it pleased

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: To shine on my contemptible estate.

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: Lo, whilst I waited on my tender lambs,

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: And to sun’s parching heat display’d my cheeks,

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: God’s mother deigned to appear to me,

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: And in a vision full of majesty

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: Will’d me to leave my base vocation

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: And free my country from calamity.

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: Her aid she promised and assured success.

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: In complete glory she reveal’d herself;

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: And, whereas I was black and swart before,

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: With those clear rays which she infused on me

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: That beauty am I blest with which you may see.

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: Ask me what question thou canst possible,

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: And I will answer unpremeditated.

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: My courage try by combat, if thou dar’st,

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: And thou shalt find that I exceed my sex.

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: Resolve on this; thou shalt be fortunate

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: If thou receive me for thy warlike mate.

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: Thou hast astonish’d me with thy high terms.

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: Only this proof I’ll of thy valour make:

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: In single combat thou shalt buckle with me,

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: And if thou vanquishest, thy words are true;

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: Otherwise I renounce all confidence.

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: I am prepared. Here is my keen-edg’d sword,

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: Deck’d with five flower-de-luces on each side,

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: The which at Touraine, in Saint Katharine’s churchyard,

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: Out of a great deal of old iron I chose forth.

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: Then come, o’ God’s name; I fear no woman.

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: And while I live, I’ll ne’er fly from a man.
[_Here they fight, and Joan la Pucelle overcomes._]

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: Stay, stay thy hands; thou art an Amazon,

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: And fightest with the sword of Deborah.

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: Christ’s Mother helps me, else I were too weak.

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: Whoe’er helps thee, ’tis thou that must help me.

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: Impatiently I burn with thy desire;

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: My heart and hands thou hast at once subdued.

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: Excellent Pucelle, if thy name be so,

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: Let me thy servant and not sovereign be.

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: ’Tis the French Dauphin sueth to thee thus.

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: I must not yield to any rites of love,

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: For my profession’s sacred from above.

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: When I have chased all thy foes from hence,

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: Then will I think upon a recompense.

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: Meantime look gracious on thy prostrate thrall.

lines.speaker: REIGNIER
lines.text: My lord, methinks, is very long in talk.

lines.speaker: REIGNIER
lines.text: ALENÇON.

lines.speaker: REIGNIER
lines.text: Doubtless he shrives this woman to her smock;

lines.speaker: REIGNIER
lines.text: Else ne’er could he so long protract his speech.

lines.speaker: REIGNIER
lines.text: Shall we disturb him, since he keeps no mean?

lines.speaker: REIGNIER
lines.text: ALENÇON.

lines.speaker: REIGNIER
lines.text: He may mean more than we poor men do know.

lines.speaker: REIGNIER
lines.text: These women are shrewd tempters with their tongues.

lines.speaker: REIGNIER
lines.text: My lord, where are you? What devise you on?

lines.speaker: REIGNIER
lines.text: Shall we give over Orleans, or no?

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: Why, no, I say. Distrustful recreants!

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: Fight till the last gasp; I will be your guard.

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: What she says I’ll confirm. We’ll fight it out.

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: Assign’d am I to be the English scourge.

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: This night the siege assuredly I’ll raise.

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: Expect Saint Martin’s summer, halcyon’s days,

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: Since I have entered into these wars.

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: Glory is like a circle in the water,

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: Which never ceaseth to enlarge itself

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: Till by broad spreading it disperse to nought.

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: With Henry’s death the English circle ends;

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: Dispersed are the glories it included.

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: Now am I like that proud insulting ship

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: Which Caesar and his fortune bare at once.

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: Was Mahomet inspired with a dove?

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: Thou with an eagle art inspired then.

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: Helen, the mother of great Constantine,

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: Nor yet Saint Philip’s daughters, were like thee.

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: Bright star of Venus, fall’n down on the earth,

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: How may I reverently worship thee enough?

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: ALENÇON.

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: Leave off delays, and let us raise the siege.

lines.speaker: REIGNIER
lines.text: Woman, do what thou canst to save our honours;

lines.speaker: REIGNIER
lines.text: Drive them from Orleans and be immortalized.

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: Presently we’ll try. Come, let’s away about it.

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: No prophet will I trust if she prove false.
[_Exeunt._]
Enter the Duke of Gloucester with his Servingmen in blue coats.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: I am come to survey the Tower this day.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Since Henry’s death, I fear, there is conveyance.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Where be these warders that they wait not here?

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Open the gates; ’tis Gloucester that calls.
[_Within_.]

lines.speaker: FIRST WARDER
lines.text: Who’s there that knocks so imperiously?

lines.speaker: FIRST SERVINGMAN
lines.text: It is the noble Duke of Gloucester.
[_Within_.]

lines.speaker: SECOND WARDER
lines.text: Whoe’er he be, you may not be let in.

lines.speaker: FIRST SERVINGMAN
lines.text: Villains, answer you so the Lord Protector?
[_Within_.]

lines.speaker: FIRST WARDER
lines.text: The Lord protect him, so we answer him.

lines.speaker: FIRST WARDER
lines.text: We do no otherwise than we are will’d.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Who willed you? Or whose will stands but mine?

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: There’s none Protector of the realm but I.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Break up the gates, I’ll be your warrantize.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Shall I be flouted thus by dunghill grooms?
[_Gloucester’s men rush at the Tower gates, and Woodville, the Lieutenant, speaks within._]

lines.speaker: WOODVILLE
lines.text: What noise is this? What traitors have we here?

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Lieutenant, is it you whose voice I hear?

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Open the gates; here’s Gloucester that would enter.

lines.speaker: WOODVILLE
lines.text: Have patience, noble Duke; I may not open;

lines.speaker: WOODVILLE
lines.text: The Cardinal of Winchester forbids.

lines.speaker: WOODVILLE
lines.text: From him I have express commandment

lines.speaker: WOODVILLE
lines.text: That thou nor none of thine shall be let in.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Faint-hearted Woodville, prizest him ’fore me?

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Arrogant Winchester, that haughty prelate

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Whom Henry, our late sovereign, ne’er could brook?

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Thou art no friend to God or to the King.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Open the gates, or I’ll shut thee out shortly.

lines.speaker: SERVINGMEN
lines.text: Open the gates unto the Lord Protector,

lines.speaker: SERVINGMEN
lines.text: Or we’ll burst them open, if that you come not quickly.
Enter to the Protector at the Tower gates Winchester and his men in tawny coats.

lines.speaker: WINCHESTER
lines.text: How now, ambitious Humphrey! What means this?

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Peel’d priest, dost thou command me to be shut out?

lines.speaker: WINCHESTER
lines.text: I do, thou most usurping proditor,

lines.speaker: WINCHESTER
lines.text: And not Protector, of the King or realm.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Stand back, thou manifest conspirator,

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Thou that contrived’st to murder our dead lord;

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Thou that giv’st whores indulgences to sin:

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: I’ll canvass thee in thy broad cardinal’s hat,

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: If thou proceed in this thy insolence.

lines.speaker: WINCHESTER
lines.text: Nay, stand thou back; I will not budge a foot.

lines.speaker: WINCHESTER
lines.text: This be Damascus, be thou cursed Cain,

lines.speaker: WINCHESTER
lines.text: To slay thy brother Abel, if thou wilt.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: I will not slay thee, but I’ll drive thee back.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Thy scarlet robes, as a child’s bearing-cloth,

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: I’ll use to carry thee out of this place.

lines.speaker: WINCHESTER
lines.text: Do what thou dar’st, I beard thee to thy face.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: What, am I dared and bearded to my face?

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Draw, men, for all this privileged place.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Blue coats to tawny coats. Priest, beware your beard;

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: I mean to tug it and to cuff you soundly.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Under my feet I’ll stamp thy cardinal’s hat;

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: In spite of Pope or dignities of church,

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Here by the cheeks I’ll drag thee up and down.

lines.speaker: WINCHESTER
lines.text: Gloucester, thou wilt answer this before the Pope.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Winchester goose, I cry, “a rope, a rope!”

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Now beat them hence; why do you let them stay?

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Thee I’ll chase hence, thou wolf in sheep’s array.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Out, tawny coats! Out, scarlet hypocrite!

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Here Gloucester’s men beat out the Cardinal’s men, and enter in the

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: hurly-burly the Mayor of London and his Officers.

lines.speaker: MAYOR
lines.text: Fie, lords, that you, being supreme magistrates,

lines.speaker: MAYOR
lines.text: Thus contumeliously should break the peace!

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Peace, Mayor! Thou know’st little of my wrongs.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Here’s Beaufort, that regards nor God nor king,

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Hath here distrain’d the Tower to his use.

lines.speaker: WINCHESTER
lines.text: Here’s Gloucester, a foe to citizens,

lines.speaker: WINCHESTER
lines.text: One that still motions war and never peace,

lines.speaker: WINCHESTER
lines.text: O’ercharging your free purses with large fines;

lines.speaker: WINCHESTER
lines.text: That seeks to overthrow religion,

lines.speaker: WINCHESTER
lines.text: Because he is Protector of the realm,

lines.speaker: WINCHESTER
lines.text: And would have armour here out of the Tower,

lines.speaker: WINCHESTER
lines.text: To crown himself king and suppress the Prince.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: I will not answer thee with words, but blows.
[_Here they skirmish again._]

lines.speaker: MAYOR
lines.text: Nought rests for me in this tumultuous strife

lines.speaker: MAYOR
lines.text: But to make open proclamation.

lines.speaker: MAYOR
lines.text: Come, officer, as loud as e’er thou canst, cry.

lines.speaker: OFFICER
lines.text: All manner of men assembled here in arms this day against God’s peace

lines.speaker: OFFICER
lines.text: and the King’s, we charge and command you, in his Highness’ name, to

lines.speaker: OFFICER
lines.text: repair to your several dwelling-places; and not to wear, handle, or use

lines.speaker: OFFICER
lines.text: any sword, weapon, or dagger, henceforward, upon pain of death.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Cardinal, I’ll be no breaker of the law;

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: But we shall meet and break our minds at large.

lines.speaker: WINCHESTER
lines.text: Gloucester, we will meet, to thy cost, be sure;

lines.speaker: WINCHESTER
lines.text: Thy heart-blood I will have for this day’s work.

lines.speaker: MAYOR
lines.text: I’ll call for clubs, if you will not away.

lines.speaker: MAYOR
lines.text: This Cardinal’s more haughty than the devil.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Mayor, farewell. Thou dost but what thou mayst.

lines.speaker: WINCHESTER
lines.text: Abominable Gloucester, guard thy head,

lines.speaker: WINCHESTER
lines.text: For I intend to have it ere long.
[_Exeunt, severally, Gloucester and Winchester with their Servingmen._]

lines.speaker: MAYOR
lines.text: See the coast clear’d, and then we will depart.

lines.speaker: MAYOR
lines.text: Good God, these nobles should such stomachs bear!

lines.speaker: MAYOR
lines.text: I myself fight not once in forty year.
[_Exeunt._]
Enter, on the walls, a Master Gunner and his Boy.

lines.speaker: MASTER GUNNER
lines.text: Sirrah, thou know’st how Orleans is besieged,

lines.speaker: MASTER GUNNER
lines.text: And how the English have the suburbs won.

lines.speaker: BOY
lines.text: Father, I know; and oft have shot at them,

lines.speaker: BOY
lines.text: Howe’er unfortunate I miss’d my aim.

lines.speaker: MASTER GUNNER
lines.text: But now thou shalt not. Be thou ruled by me.

lines.speaker: MASTER GUNNER
lines.text: Chief master-gunner am I of this town;

lines.speaker: MASTER GUNNER
lines.text: Something I must do to procure me grace.

lines.speaker: MASTER GUNNER
lines.text: The Prince’s espials have informed me

lines.speaker: MASTER GUNNER
lines.text: How the English, in the suburbs close intrench’d,

lines.speaker: MASTER GUNNER
lines.text: Wont, through a secret grate of iron bars

lines.speaker: MASTER GUNNER
lines.text: In yonder tower, to overpeer the city,

lines.speaker: MASTER GUNNER
lines.text: And thence discover how with most advantage

lines.speaker: MASTER GUNNER
lines.text: They may vex us with shot or with assault.

lines.speaker: MASTER GUNNER
lines.text: To intercept this inconvenience,

lines.speaker: MASTER GUNNER
lines.text: A piece of ordnance ’gainst it I have placed

lines.speaker: MASTER GUNNER
lines.text: And even these three days have I watch’d,

lines.speaker: MASTER GUNNER
lines.text: If I could see them.

lines.speaker: MASTER GUNNER
lines.text: Now do thou watch, for I can stay no longer.

lines.speaker: MASTER GUNNER
lines.text: If thou spy’st any, run and bring me word;

lines.speaker: MASTER GUNNER
lines.text: And thou shalt find me at the Governor’s.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: BOY
lines.text: Father, I warrant you; take you no care;

lines.speaker: BOY
lines.text: I’ll never trouble you if I may spy them.
[_Exit._]
Enter, on the turrets, Salisbury and Talbot, Sir William Glansdale, Sir Thomas Gargrave and others.

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: Talbot, my life, my joy, again return’d!

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: How wert thou handled, being prisoner?

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: Or by what means got’st thou to be releas’d?

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: Discourse, I prithee, on this turret’s top.

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: The Duke of Bedford had a prisoner

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Call’d the brave Lord Ponton de Santrailles;

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: For him was I exchanged and ransomed.

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: But with a baser man of arms by far

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Once in contempt they would have barter’d me,

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Which I disdaining scorn’d, and craved death

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Rather than I would be so vile-esteem’d.

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: In fine, redeem’d I was as I desired.

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: But O, the treacherous Fastolf wounds my heart,

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Whom with my bare fists I would execute

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: If I now had him brought into my power.

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: Yet tell’st thou not how thou wert entertain’d.

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: With scoffs and scorns and contumelious taunts.

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: In open market-place produced they me

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: To be a public spectacle to all.

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Here, said they, is the terror of the French,

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: The scarecrow that affrights our children so.

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Then broke I from the officers that led me,

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: And with my nails digg’d stones out of the ground

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: To hurl at the beholders of my shame.

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: My grisly countenance made others fly;

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: None durst come near for fear of sudden death.

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: In iron walls they deem’d me not secure;

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: So great fear of my name ’mongst them were spread

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: That they supposed I could rend bars of steel

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: And spurn in pieces posts of adamant.

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Wherefore a guard of chosen shot I had,

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: That walk’d about me every minute while;

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: And if I did but stir out of my bed,

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Ready they were to shoot me to the heart.
Enter the Boy with a linstock.

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: I grieve to hear what torments you endured,

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: But we will be revenged sufficiently.

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: Now it is supper-time in Orleans.

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: Here, through this grate, I count each one

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: And view the Frenchmen how they fortify.

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: Let us look in; the sight will much delight thee.

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: Sir Thomas Gargrave and Sir William Glansdale,

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: Let me have your express opinions

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: Where is best place to make our battery next.

lines.speaker: GARGRAVE
lines.text: I think, at the north gate, for there stand lords.

lines.speaker: GLANSDALE
lines.text: And I, here, at the bulwark of the bridge.

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: For aught I see, this city must be famish’d,

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Or with light skirmishes enfeebled.

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Here they shoot, and Salisbury and Gargrave fall down.

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: O Lord, have mercy on us, wretched sinners!

lines.speaker: GARGRAVE
lines.text: O Lord, have mercy on me, woeful man!

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: What chance is this that suddenly hath cross’d us?

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Speak, Salisbury; at least, if thou canst speak!

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: How far’st thou, mirror of all martial men?

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: One of thy eyes and thy cheek’s side struck off!

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Accursed tower, accursed fatal hand

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: That hath contrived this woeful tragedy!

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: In thirteen battles Salisbury o’ercame;

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Henry the Fifth he first train’d to the wars;

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Whilst any trump did sound, or drum struck up,

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: His sword did ne’er leave striking in the field.

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Yet liv’st thou, Salisbury? Though thy speech doth fail,

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: One eye thou hast to look to heaven for grace.

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: The sun with one eye vieweth all the world.

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Heaven, be thou gracious to none alive,

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: If Salisbury wants mercy at thy hands!

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Sir Thomas Gargrave, hast thou any life?

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Speak unto Talbot; nay, look up to him.

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Bear hence his body; I will help to bury it.
[_Exeunt some with the body of Gargrave._]

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Salisbury, cheer thy spirit with this comfort,

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Thou shalt not die whiles—

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: He beckons with his hand and smiles on me,

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: As who should say “When I am dead and gone,

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Remember to avenge me on the French.”

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Plantagenet, I will; and, like thee, Nero,

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Play on the lute, beholding the towns burn.

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Wretched shall France be only in thy name.
[_Here an alarum, and it thunders and lightens._]

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: What stir is this? What tumult’s in the heavens?

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Whence cometh this alarum and the noise?
Enter a Messenger.

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: My lord, my lord, the French have gather’d head.

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: The Dauphin, with one Joan la Pucelle join’d,

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: A holy prophetess new risen up,

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: Is come with a great power to raise the siege.
[_Here Salisbury lifteth himself up and groans._]

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Hear, hear how dying Salisbury doth groan;

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: It irks his heart he cannot be revenged.

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Frenchmen, I’ll be a Salisbury to you.

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Pucelle or puzel, dolphin or dogfish,

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Your hearts I’ll stamp out with my horse’s heels

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: And make a quagmire of your mingled brains.

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Convey we Salisbury into his tent,

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: And then we’ll try what these dastard Frenchmen dare.
[_Alarum. Exeunt._]
Here an alarum again, and Talbot pursueth the Dauphin and driveth him; then enter Joan la Pucelle, driving Englishmen before her, and exit after them. Then re-enter Talbot.

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Where is my strength, my valour, and my force?

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Our English troops retire, I cannot stay them.

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: A woman clad in armour chaseth them.
Enter La Pucelle.

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Here, here she comes. I’ll have a bout with thee;

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Devil or devil’s dam, I’ll conjure thee.

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Blood will I draw on thee, thou art a witch,

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: And straightway give thy soul to him thou serv’st.

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: Come, come, ’tis only I that must disgrace thee.
[_Here they fight._]

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Heavens, can you suffer hell so to prevail?

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: My breast I’ll burst with straining of my courage,

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: And from my shoulders crack my arms asunder,

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: But I will chastise this high-minded strumpet.
[_They fight again._]

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: Talbot, farewell; thy hour is not yet come.

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: I must go victual Orleans forthwith.
[_A short alarum. Then enter the town with soldiers._]

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: O’ertake me, if thou canst. I scorn thy strength.

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: Go, go, cheer up thy hungry-starved men;

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: Help Salisbury to make his testament.

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: This day is ours, as many more shall be.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: My thoughts are whirled like a potter’s wheel;

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: I know not where I am, nor what I do.

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: A witch by fear, not force, like Hannibal,

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Drives back our troops and conquers as she lists.

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: So bees with smoke and doves with noisome stench

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Are from their hives and houses driven away.

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: They call’d us for our fierceness, English dogs;

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Now like to whelps we crying run away.
[_A short alarum._]

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Hark, countrymen, either renew the fight,

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Or tear the lions out of England’s coat;

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Renounce your soil, give sheep in lions’ stead.

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Sheep run not half so treacherous from the wolf,

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Or horse or oxen from the leopard,

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: As you fly from your oft-subdued slaves.
[_Alarum. Here another skirmish._]

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: It will not be! Retire into your trenches.

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: You all consented unto Salisbury’s death,

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: For none would strike a stroke in his revenge.

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Pucelle is enter’d into Orleans,

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: In spite of us or aught that we could do.

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: O, would I were to die with Salisbury!

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: The shame hereof will make me hide my head.
[_Exit Talbot. Alarum; retreat._]
Flourish. Enter on the walls La Pucelle, Charles, Reignier, Alençon and Soldiers.

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: Advance our waving colours on the walls;

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: Rescued is Orleans from the English.

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: Thus Joan la Pucelle hath perform’d her word.

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: Divinest creature, Astraea’s daughter,

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: How shall I honour thee for this success?

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: Thy promises are like Adonis’ gardens

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: That one day bloom’d and fruitful were the next.

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: France, triumph in thy glorious prophetess!

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: Recover’d is the town of Orleans.

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: More blessed hap did ne’er befall our state.

lines.speaker: REIGNIER
lines.text: Why ring not bells aloud throughout the town?

lines.speaker: REIGNIER
lines.text: Dauphin, command the citizens make bonfires

lines.speaker: REIGNIER
lines.text: And feast and banquet in the open streets

lines.speaker: REIGNIER
lines.text: To celebrate the joy that God hath given us.

lines.speaker: REIGNIER
lines.text: ALENÇON.

lines.speaker: REIGNIER
lines.text: All France will be replete with mirth and joy

lines.speaker: REIGNIER
lines.text: When they shall hear how we have play’d the men.

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: ’Tis Joan, not we, by whom the day is won;

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: For which I will divide my crown with her,

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: And all the priests and friars in my realm

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: Shall in procession sing her endless praise.

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: A statelier pyramis to her I’ll rear

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: Than Rhodope’s of Memphis ever was;

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: In memory of her when she is dead,

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: Her ashes, in an urn more precious

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: Than the rich-jewel’d coffer of Darius,

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: Transported shall be at high festivals

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: Before the kings and queens of France.

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: No longer on Saint Denis will we cry,

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: But Joan la Pucelle shall be France’s saint.

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: Come in, and let us banquet royally

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: After this golden day of victory.
[_Flourish. Exeunt._]
Enter a Sergeant of a band, with two Sentinels.

lines.speaker: SERGEANT
lines.text: Sirs, take your places and be vigilant.

lines.speaker: SERGEANT
lines.text: If any noise or soldier you perceive

lines.speaker: SERGEANT
lines.text: Near to the walls, by some apparent sign

lines.speaker: SERGEANT
lines.text: Let us have knowledge at the court of guard.

lines.speaker: FIRST SENTINEL
lines.text: Sergeant, you shall.
[_Exit Sergeant._]

lines.speaker: FIRST SENTINEL
lines.text: Thus are poor servitors,

lines.speaker: FIRST SENTINEL
lines.text: When others sleep upon their quiet beds,

lines.speaker: FIRST SENTINEL
lines.text: Constrain’d to watch in darkness, rain, and cold.
Enter Talbot, Bedford, Burgundy, and forces, with scaling-ladders.

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Lord Regent, and redoubted Burgundy,

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: By whose approach the regions of Artois,

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Walloon and Picardy are friends to us,

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: This happy night the Frenchmen are secure,

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Having all day caroused and banqueted.

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Embrace we then this opportunity,

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: As fitting best to quittance their deceit

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Contriv’d by art and baleful sorcery.

lines.speaker: BEDFORD
lines.text: Coward of France, how much he wrongs his fame,

lines.speaker: BEDFORD
lines.text: Despairing of his own arm’s fortitude,

lines.speaker: BEDFORD
lines.text: To join with witches and the help of hell!

lines.speaker: BURGUNDY
lines.text: Traitors have never other company.

lines.speaker: BURGUNDY
lines.text: But what’s that Pucelle whom they term so pure?

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: A maid, they say.

lines.speaker: BEDFORD
lines.text: A maid! And be so martial!

lines.speaker: BURGUNDY
lines.text: Pray God she prove not masculine ere long,

lines.speaker: BURGUNDY
lines.text: If underneath the standard of the French

lines.speaker: BURGUNDY
lines.text: She carry armour as she hath begun.

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Well, let them practice and converse with spirits.

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: God is our fortress, in whose conquering name

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Let us resolve to scale their flinty bulwarks.

lines.speaker: BEDFORD
lines.text: Ascend, brave Talbot; we will follow thee.

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Not all together. Better far, I guess,

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: That we do make our entrance several ways,

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: That if it chance the one of us do fail,

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: The other yet may rise against their force.

lines.speaker: BEDFORD
lines.text: Agreed. I’ll to yond corner.

lines.speaker: BURGUNDY
lines.text: And I to this.

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: And here will Talbot mount, or make his grave.

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Now, Salisbury, for thee, and for the right

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Of English Henry, shall this night appear

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: How much in duty I am bound to both.

lines.speaker: SENTINEL
lines.text: Arm! Arm! The enemy doth make assault!
[_Cry: “St George,” “A Talbot!”_]

lines.speaker: SENTINEL
lines.text: The French leap over the walls in their shirts. Enter several ways the

lines.speaker: SENTINEL
lines.text: Bastard of Orleans, Alençon and Reignier, half ready and half unready.

lines.speaker: SENTINEL
lines.text: ALENÇON.

lines.speaker: SENTINEL
lines.text: How now, my lords? What, all unready so?

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: Unready! Ay, and glad we ’scap’d so well.

lines.speaker: REIGNIER
lines.text: ’Twas time, I trow, to wake and leave our beds,

lines.speaker: REIGNIER
lines.text: Hearing alarums at our chamber-doors.

lines.speaker: REIGNIER
lines.text: ALENÇON.

lines.speaker: REIGNIER
lines.text: Of all exploits since first I follow’d arms

lines.speaker: REIGNIER
lines.text: Ne’er heard I of a warlike enterprise

lines.speaker: REIGNIER
lines.text: More venturous or desperate than this.

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: I think this Talbot be a fiend of hell.

lines.speaker: REIGNIER
lines.text: If not of hell, the heavens, sure, favour him.

lines.speaker: REIGNIER
lines.text: ALENÇON.

lines.speaker: REIGNIER
lines.text: Here cometh Charles. I marvel how he sped.
Enter Charles and La Pucelle.

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: Tut, holy Joan was his defensive guard.

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: Is this thy cunning, thou deceitful dame?

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: Didst thou at first, to flatter us withal,

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: Make us partakers of a little gain,

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: That now our loss might be ten times so much?

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: Wherefore is Charles impatient with his friend?

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: At all times will you have my power alike?

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: Sleeping or waking, must I still prevail,

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: Or will you blame and lay the fault on me?

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: Improvident soldiers, had your watch been good,

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: This sudden mischief never could have fall’n.

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: Duke of Alençon, this was your default,

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: That, being captain of the watch tonight,

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: Did look no better to that weighty charge.

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: ALENÇON.

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: Had all your quarters been as safely kept

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: As that whereof I had the government,

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: We had not been thus shamefully surprised.

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: Mine was secure.

lines.speaker: REIGNIER
lines.text: And so was mine, my lord.

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: And for myself, most part of all this night,

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: Within her quarter and mine own precinct

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: I was employ’d in passing to and fro

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: About relieving of the sentinels.

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: Then how or which way should they first break in?

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: Question, my lords, no further of the case,

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: How or which way; ’tis sure they found some place

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: But weakly guarded, where the breach was made.

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: And now there rests no other shift but this:

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: To gather our soldiers, scattered and dispersed,

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: And lay new platforms to endamage them.
Alarum. Enter an  English Soldier, crying “A Talbot! A Talbot!” They fly, leaving their clothes behind.

lines.speaker: SOLDIER
lines.text: I’ll be so bold to take what they have left.

lines.speaker: SOLDIER
lines.text: The cry of “Talbot” serves me for a sword;

lines.speaker: SOLDIER
lines.text: For I have loaden me with many spoils,

lines.speaker: SOLDIER
lines.text: Using no other weapon but his name.
[_Exit._]
Enter Talbot, Bedford, Burgundy, a Captain and others.

lines.speaker: BEDFORD
lines.text: The day begins to break, and night is fled,

lines.speaker: BEDFORD
lines.text: Whose pitchy mantle over-veil’d the earth.

lines.speaker: BEDFORD
lines.text: Here sound retreat and cease our hot pursuit.
[_Retreat sounded._]

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Bring forth the body of old Salisbury,

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: And here advance it in the market-place,

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: The middle centre of this cursed town.

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Dead March. Enter with the body of Salisbury.

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Now have I paid my vow unto his soul;

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: For every drop of blood was drawn from him

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: There hath at least five Frenchmen died tonight.

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: And that hereafter ages may behold

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: What ruin happen’d in revenge of him,

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Within their chiefest temple I’ll erect

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: A tomb, wherein his corpse shall be interr’d;

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Upon the which, that everyone may read,

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Shall be engraved the sack of Orleans,

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: The treacherous manner of his mournful death

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: And what a terror he had been to France.
[_Exit Funeral._]

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: But, lords, in all our bloody massacre,

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: I muse we met not with the Dauphin’s grace,

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: His new-come champion, virtuous Joan of Arc,

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Nor any of his false confederates.

lines.speaker: BEDFORD
lines.text: ’Tis thought, Lord Talbot, when the fight began,

lines.speaker: BEDFORD
lines.text: Rous’d on the sudden from their drowsy beds,

lines.speaker: BEDFORD
lines.text: They did amongst the troops of armed men

lines.speaker: BEDFORD
lines.text: Leap o’er the walls for refuge in the field.

lines.speaker: BURGUNDY
lines.text: Myself, as far as I could well discern

lines.speaker: BURGUNDY
lines.text: For smoke and dusky vapors of the night,

lines.speaker: BURGUNDY
lines.text: Am sure I scared the Dauphin and his trull,

lines.speaker: BURGUNDY
lines.text: When arm in arm they both came swiftly running,

lines.speaker: BURGUNDY
lines.text: Like to a pair of loving turtle-doves

lines.speaker: BURGUNDY
lines.text: That could not live asunder day or night.

lines.speaker: BURGUNDY
lines.text: After that things are set in order here,

lines.speaker: BURGUNDY
lines.text: We’ll follow them with all the power we have.
Enter a Messenger.

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: All hail, my lords! Which of this princely train

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: Call ye the warlike Talbot, for his acts

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: So much applauded through the realm of France?

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Here is the Talbot. Who would speak with him?

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: The virtuous lady, Countess of Auvergne,

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: With modesty admiring thy renown,

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: By me entreats, great lord, thou wouldst vouchsafe

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: To visit her poor castle where she lies,

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: That she may boast she hath beheld the man

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: Whose glory fills the world with loud report.

lines.speaker: BURGUNDY
lines.text: Is it even so? Nay, then I see our wars

lines.speaker: BURGUNDY
lines.text: Will turn unto a peaceful comic sport,

lines.speaker: BURGUNDY
lines.text: When ladies crave to be encounter’d with.

lines.speaker: BURGUNDY
lines.text: You may not, my lord, despise her gentle suit.

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Ne’er trust me then; for when a world of men

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Could not prevail with all their oratory,

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Yet hath a woman’s kindness over-ruled.

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: And therefore tell her I return great thanks,

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: And in submission will attend on her.

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Will not your honours bear me company?

lines.speaker: BEDFORD
lines.text: No, truly, it is more than manners will;

lines.speaker: BEDFORD
lines.text: And I have heard it said, unbidden guests

lines.speaker: BEDFORD
lines.text: Are often welcomest when they are gone.

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Well then, alone, since there’s no remedy,

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: I mean to prove this lady’s courtesy.

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Come hither, Captain. [_Whispers_.] You perceive my mind?

lines.speaker: CAPTAIN
lines.text: I do, my lord, and mean accordingly.
[_Exeunt._]
Enter the Countess and her Porter.

lines.speaker: COUNTESS
lines.text: Porter, remember what I gave in charge;

lines.speaker: COUNTESS
lines.text: And when you have done so, bring the keys to me.

lines.speaker: PORTER
lines.text: Madam, I will.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: COUNTESS
lines.text: The plot is laid. If all things fall out right,

lines.speaker: COUNTESS
lines.text: I shall as famous be by this exploit

lines.speaker: COUNTESS
lines.text: As Scythian Tomyris by Cyrus’ death.

lines.speaker: COUNTESS
lines.text: Great is the rumour of this dreadful knight,

lines.speaker: COUNTESS
lines.text: And his achievements of no less account.

lines.speaker: COUNTESS
lines.text: Fain would mine eyes be witness with mine ears,

lines.speaker: COUNTESS
lines.text: To give their censure of these rare reports.
Enter Messenger and Talbot.

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: Madam, according as your ladyship desired,

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: By message craved, so is Lord Talbot come.

lines.speaker: COUNTESS
lines.text: And he is welcome. What, is this the man?

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: Madam, it is.

lines.speaker: COUNTESS
lines.text: Is this the scourge of France?

lines.speaker: COUNTESS
lines.text: Is this the Talbot, so much fear’d abroad

lines.speaker: COUNTESS
lines.text: That with his name the mothers still their babes?

lines.speaker: COUNTESS
lines.text: I see report is fabulous and false.

lines.speaker: COUNTESS
lines.text: I thought I should have seen some Hercules,

lines.speaker: COUNTESS
lines.text: A second Hector, for his grim aspect,

lines.speaker: COUNTESS
lines.text: And large proportion of his strong-knit limbs.

lines.speaker: COUNTESS
lines.text: Alas, this is a child, a silly dwarf!

lines.speaker: COUNTESS
lines.text: It cannot be this weak and writhled shrimp

lines.speaker: COUNTESS
lines.text: Should strike such terror to his enemies.

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Madam, I have been bold to trouble you;

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: But since your ladyship is not at leisure,

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: I’ll sort some other time to visit you.

lines.speaker: COUNTESS
lines.text: What means he now? Go ask him whither he goes.

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: Stay, my Lord Talbot, for my lady craves

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: To know the cause of your abrupt departure.

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Marry, for that she’s in a wrong belief,

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: I go to certify her Talbot’s here.
Enter Porter with keys.

lines.speaker: COUNTESS
lines.text: If thou be he, then art thou prisoner.

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Prisoner! To whom?

lines.speaker: COUNTESS
lines.text: To me, blood-thirsty lord;

lines.speaker: COUNTESS
lines.text: And for that cause I train’d thee to my house.

lines.speaker: COUNTESS
lines.text: Long time thy shadow hath been thrall to me,

lines.speaker: COUNTESS
lines.text: For in my gallery thy picture hangs.

lines.speaker: COUNTESS
lines.text: But now the substance shall endure the like,

lines.speaker: COUNTESS
lines.text: And I will chain these legs and arms of thine,

lines.speaker: COUNTESS
lines.text: That hast by tyranny these many years

lines.speaker: COUNTESS
lines.text: Wasted our country, slain our citizens,

lines.speaker: COUNTESS
lines.text: And sent our sons and husbands captivate.

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Ha, ha, ha!

lines.speaker: COUNTESS
lines.text: Laughest thou, wretch? Thy mirth shall turn to moan.

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: I laugh to see your ladyship so fond

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: To think that you have aught but Talbot’s shadow

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Whereon to practice your severity.

lines.speaker: COUNTESS
lines.text: Why, art not thou the man?

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: I am indeed.

lines.speaker: COUNTESS
lines.text: Then have I substance too.

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: No, no, I am but shadow of myself.

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: You are deceived, my substance is not here;

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: For what you see is but the smallest part

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: And least proportion of humanity.

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: I tell you, madam, were the whole frame here,

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: It is of such a spacious lofty pitch

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Your roof were not sufficient to contain ’t.

lines.speaker: COUNTESS
lines.text: This is a riddling merchant for the nonce;

lines.speaker: COUNTESS
lines.text: He will be here, and yet he is not here.

lines.speaker: COUNTESS
lines.text: How can these contrarieties agree?

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: That will I show you presently.

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Winds his horn. Drums strike up; a peal of ordnance. Enter Soldiers.

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: How say you, madam? Are you now persuaded

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: That Talbot is but shadow of himself?

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: These are his substance, sinews, arms and strength,

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: With which he yoketh your rebellious necks,

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Razeth your cities and subverts your towns,

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: And in a moment makes them desolate.

lines.speaker: COUNTESS
lines.text: Victorious Talbot, pardon my abuse.

lines.speaker: COUNTESS
lines.text: I find thou art no less than fame hath bruited,

lines.speaker: COUNTESS
lines.text: And more than may be gather’d by thy shape.

lines.speaker: COUNTESS
lines.text: Let my presumption not provoke thy wrath,

lines.text: For I am sorry that with reverence

lines.text: I did not entertain thee as thou art.

lines.text: Be not dismay’d, fair lady, nor misconster

lines.text: The mind of Talbot, as you did mistake
