lines.text: The outward composition of his body.

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: What you have done hath not offended me;

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Nor other satisfaction do I crave

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: But only, with your patience, that we may

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Taste of your wine and see what cates you have,

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: For soldiers’ stomachs always serve them well.

lines.speaker: COUNTESS
lines.text: With all my heart, and think me honoured

lines.speaker: COUNTESS
lines.text: To feast so great a warrior in my house.
[_Exeunt._]
Enter the Earls of Somerset, Suffolk, and Warwick; Richard Plantagenet, Vernon and another Lawyer.

lines.speaker: PLANTAGENET
lines.text: Great lords and gentlemen, what means this silence?

lines.speaker: PLANTAGENET
lines.text: Dare no man answer in a case of truth?

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Within the Temple Hall we were too loud;

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: The garden here is more convenient.

lines.speaker: PLANTAGENET
lines.text: Then say at once if I maintain’d the truth;

lines.speaker: PLANTAGENET
lines.text: Or else was wrangling Somerset in th’ error?

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Faith, I have been a truant in the law

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: And never yet could frame my will to it;

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: And therefore frame the law unto my will.

lines.speaker: SOMERSET
lines.text: Judge you, my Lord of Warwick, then, between us.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Between two hawks, which flies the higher pitch;

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Between two dogs, which hath the deeper mouth;

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Between two blades, which bears the better temper;

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Between two horses, which doth bear him best;

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Between two girls, which hath the merriest eye;

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: I have perhaps some shallow spirit of judgement;

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: But in these nice sharp quillets of the law,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Good faith, I am no wiser than a daw.

lines.speaker: PLANTAGENET
lines.text: Tut, tut, here is a mannerly forbearance!

lines.speaker: PLANTAGENET
lines.text: The truth appears so naked on my side

lines.speaker: PLANTAGENET
lines.text: That any purblind eye may find it out.

lines.speaker: SOMERSET
lines.text: And on my side it is so well apparell’d,

lines.speaker: SOMERSET
lines.text: So clear, so shining and so evident,

lines.speaker: SOMERSET
lines.text: That it will glimmer through a blind man’s eye.

lines.speaker: PLANTAGENET
lines.text: Since you are tongue-tied and so loath to speak,

lines.speaker: PLANTAGENET
lines.text: In dumb significants proclaim your thoughts:

lines.speaker: PLANTAGENET
lines.text: Let him that is a true-born gentleman

lines.speaker: PLANTAGENET
lines.text: And stands upon the honour of his birth,

lines.speaker: PLANTAGENET
lines.text: If he suppose that I have pleaded truth,

lines.speaker: PLANTAGENET
lines.text: From off this brier pluck a white rose with me.

lines.speaker: SOMERSET
lines.text: Let him that is no coward nor no flatterer,

lines.speaker: SOMERSET
lines.text: But dare maintain the party of the truth,

lines.speaker: SOMERSET
lines.text: Pluck a red rose from off this thorn with me.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: I love no colours, and without all colour

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Of base insinuating flattery

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: I pluck this white rose with Plantagenet.

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: I pluck this red rose with young Somerset,

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: And say withal I think he held the right.

lines.speaker: VERNON
lines.text: Stay, lords and gentlemen, and pluck no more

lines.speaker: VERNON
lines.text: Till you conclude that he upon whose side

lines.speaker: VERNON
lines.text: The fewest roses are cropp’d from the tree

lines.speaker: VERNON
lines.text: Shall yield the other in the right opinion.

lines.speaker: SOMERSET
lines.text: Good Master Vernon, it is well objected:

lines.speaker: SOMERSET
lines.text: If I have fewest, I subscribe in silence.

lines.speaker: PLANTAGENET
lines.text: And I.

lines.speaker: VERNON
lines.text: Then for the truth and plainness of the case,

lines.speaker: VERNON
lines.text: I pluck this pale and maiden blossom here,

lines.speaker: VERNON
lines.text: Giving my verdict on the white rose side.

lines.speaker: SOMERSET
lines.text: Prick not your finger as you pluck it off,

lines.speaker: SOMERSET
lines.text: Lest, bleeding, you do paint the white rose red,

lines.speaker: SOMERSET
lines.text: And fall on my side so against your will.

lines.speaker: VERNON
lines.text: If I, my lord, for my opinion bleed,

lines.speaker: VERNON
lines.text: Opinion shall be surgeon to my hurt

lines.speaker: VERNON
lines.text: And keep me on the side where still I am.

lines.speaker: SOMERSET
lines.text: Well, well, come on, who else?

lines.speaker: LAWYER
lines.text: Unless my study and my books be false,
[_To Somerset._]

lines.speaker: LAWYER
lines.text: The argument you held was wrong in law;

lines.speaker: LAWYER
lines.text: In sign whereof I pluck a white rose too.

lines.speaker: PLANTAGENET
lines.text: Now, Somerset, where is your argument?

lines.speaker: SOMERSET
lines.text: Here in my scabbard, meditating that

lines.speaker: SOMERSET
lines.text: Shall dye your white rose in a bloody red.

lines.speaker: PLANTAGENET
lines.text: Meantime your cheeks do counterfeit our roses;

lines.speaker: PLANTAGENET
lines.text: For pale they look with fear, as witnessing

lines.speaker: PLANTAGENET
lines.text: The truth on our side.

lines.speaker: SOMERSET
lines.text: No, Plantagenet,

lines.speaker: SOMERSET
lines.text: ’Tis not for fear but anger that thy cheeks

lines.speaker: SOMERSET
lines.text: Blush for pure shame to counterfeit our roses,

lines.speaker: SOMERSET
lines.text: And yet thy tongue will not confess thy error.

lines.speaker: PLANTAGENET
lines.text: Hath not thy rose a canker, Somerset?

lines.speaker: SOMERSET
lines.text: Hath not thy rose a thorn, Plantagenet?

lines.speaker: PLANTAGENET
lines.text: Ay, sharp and piercing, to maintain his truth;

lines.speaker: PLANTAGENET
lines.text: Whiles thy consuming canker eats his falsehood.

lines.speaker: SOMERSET
lines.text: Well, I’ll find friends to wear my bleeding roses,

lines.speaker: SOMERSET
lines.text: That shall maintain what I have said is true,

lines.speaker: SOMERSET
lines.text: Where false Plantagenet dare not be seen.

lines.speaker: PLANTAGENET
lines.text: Now, by this maiden blossom in my hand,

lines.speaker: PLANTAGENET
lines.text: I scorn thee and thy fashion, peevish boy.

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Turn not thy scorns this way, Plantagenet.

lines.speaker: PLANTAGENET
lines.text: Proud Pole, I will, and scorn both him and thee.

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: I’ll turn my part thereof into thy throat.

lines.speaker: SOMERSET
lines.text: Away, away, good William de la Pole!

lines.speaker: SOMERSET
lines.text: We grace the yeoman by conversing with him.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Now, by God’s will, thou wrong’st him, Somerset;

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: His grandfather was Lionel Duke of Clarence,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Third son to the third Edward King of England.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Spring crestless yeomen from so deep a root?

lines.speaker: PLANTAGENET
lines.text: He bears him on the place’s privilege,

lines.speaker: PLANTAGENET
lines.text: Or durst not for his craven heart, say thus.

lines.speaker: SOMERSET
lines.text: By Him that made me, I’ll maintain my words

lines.speaker: SOMERSET
lines.text: On any plot of ground in Christendom.

lines.speaker: SOMERSET
lines.text: Was not thy father, Richard Earl of Cambridge,

lines.speaker: SOMERSET
lines.text: For treason executed in our late king’s days?

lines.speaker: SOMERSET
lines.text: And, by his treason, stand’st not thou attainted,

lines.speaker: SOMERSET
lines.text: Corrupted, and exempt from ancient gentry?

lines.speaker: SOMERSET
lines.text: His trespass yet lives guilty in thy blood;

lines.speaker: SOMERSET
lines.text: And, till thou be restored, thou art a yeoman.

lines.speaker: PLANTAGENET
lines.text: My father was attached, not attainted,

lines.speaker: PLANTAGENET
lines.text: Condemn’d to die for treason, but no traitor;

lines.speaker: PLANTAGENET
lines.text: And that I’ll prove on better men than Somerset,

lines.speaker: PLANTAGENET
lines.text: Were growing time once ripen’d to my will.

lines.speaker: PLANTAGENET
lines.text: For your partaker Pole and you yourself,

lines.speaker: PLANTAGENET
lines.text: I’ll note you in my book of memory,

lines.speaker: PLANTAGENET
lines.text: To scourge you for this apprehension.

lines.speaker: PLANTAGENET
lines.text: Look to it well, and say you are well warn’d.

lines.speaker: SOMERSET
lines.text: Ah, thou shalt find us ready for thee still;

lines.speaker: SOMERSET
lines.text: And know us by these colours for thy foes,

lines.speaker: SOMERSET
lines.text: For these my friends in spite of thee shall wear.

lines.speaker: PLANTAGENET
lines.text: And, by my soul, this pale and angry rose,

lines.speaker: PLANTAGENET
lines.text: As cognizance of my blood-drinking hate,

lines.speaker: PLANTAGENET
lines.text: Will I for ever and my faction wear,

lines.speaker: PLANTAGENET
lines.text: Until it wither with me to my grave,

lines.speaker: PLANTAGENET
lines.text: Or flourish to the height of my degree.

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Go forward, and be chok’d with thy ambition!

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: And so farewell until I meet thee next.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: SOMERSET
lines.text: Have with thee, Pole. Farewell, ambitious Richard.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: PLANTAGENET
lines.text: How I am braved and must perforce endure it!

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: This blot that they object against your house

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Shall be wiped out in the next parliament

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Call’d for the truce of Winchester and Gloucester;

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: And if thou be not then created York,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: I will not live to be accounted Warwick.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Meantime, in signal of my love to thee,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Against proud Somerset and William Pole,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Will I upon thy party wear this rose.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: And here I prophesy: this brawl today,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Grown to this faction in the Temple Garden,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Shall send between the Red Rose and the White

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: A thousand souls to death and deadly night.

lines.speaker: PLANTAGENET
lines.text: Good Master Vernon, I am bound to you,

lines.speaker: PLANTAGENET
lines.text: That you on my behalf would pluck a flower.

lines.speaker: VERNON
lines.text: In your behalf still will I wear the same.

lines.speaker: LAWYER
lines.text: And so will I.

lines.speaker: PLANTAGENET
lines.text: Thanks, gentlemen.

lines.speaker: PLANTAGENET
lines.text: Come, let us four to dinner. I dare say

lines.speaker: PLANTAGENET
lines.text: This quarrel will drink blood another day.
[_Exeunt._]
Enter Mortimer, brought in a chair, and Jailers.

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: Kind keepers of my weak decaying age,

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: Let dying Mortimer here rest himself.

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: Even like a man new haled from the rack,

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: So fare my limbs with long imprisonment;

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: And these gray locks, the pursuivants of death,

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: Nestor-like aged in an age of care,

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: Argue the end of Edmund Mortimer.

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: These eyes, like lamps whose wasting oil is spent,

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: Wax dim, as drawing to their exigent;

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: Weak shoulders, overborne with burdening grief,

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: And pithless arms, like to a wither’d vine

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: That droops his sapless branches to the ground.

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: Yet are these feet, whose strengthless stay is numb,

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: Unable to support this lump of clay,

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: Swift-winged with desire to get a grave,

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: As witting I no other comfort have.

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: But tell me, keeper, will my nephew come?

lines.speaker: FIRST JAILER
lines.text: Richard Plantagenet, my lord, will come.

lines.speaker: FIRST JAILER
lines.text: We sent unto the Temple, unto his chamber,

lines.speaker: FIRST JAILER
lines.text: And answer was return’d that he will come.

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: Enough. My soul shall then be satisfied.

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: Poor gentleman, his wrong doth equal mine.

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: Since Henry Monmouth first began to reign,

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: Before whose glory I was great in arms,

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: This loathsome sequestration have I had;

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: And even since then hath Richard been obscured,

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: Deprived of honour and inheritance.

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: But now the arbitrator of despairs,

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: Just Death, kind umpire of men’s miseries,

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: With sweet enlargement doth dismiss me hence.

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: I would his troubles likewise were expired,

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: That so he might recover what was lost.
Enter Richard Plantagenet.

lines.speaker: FIRST JAILER
lines.text: My lord, your loving nephew now is come.

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: Richard Plantagenet, my friend, is he come?

lines.speaker: PLANTAGENET
lines.text: Ay, noble uncle, thus ignobly used,

lines.speaker: PLANTAGENET
lines.text: Your nephew, late despised Richard, comes.

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: Direct mine arms I may embrace his neck

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: And in his bosom spend my latter gasp.

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: O, tell me when my lips do touch his cheeks,

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: That I may kindly give one fainting kiss.

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: And now declare, sweet stem from York’s great stock,

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: Why didst thou say of late thou wert despised?

lines.speaker: PLANTAGENET
lines.text: First, lean thine aged back against mine arm,

lines.speaker: PLANTAGENET
lines.text: And, in that ease, I’ll tell thee my disease.

lines.speaker: PLANTAGENET
lines.text: This day, in argument upon a case,

lines.speaker: PLANTAGENET
lines.text: Some words there grew ’twixt Somerset and me;

lines.speaker: PLANTAGENET
lines.text: Among which terms he used his lavish tongue

lines.speaker: PLANTAGENET
lines.text: And did upbraid me with my father’s death;

lines.speaker: PLANTAGENET
lines.text: Which obloquy set bars before my tongue,

lines.speaker: PLANTAGENET
lines.text: Else with the like I had requited him.

lines.speaker: PLANTAGENET
lines.text: Therefore, good uncle, for my father’s sake,

lines.speaker: PLANTAGENET
lines.text: In honour of a true Plantagenet,

lines.speaker: PLANTAGENET
lines.text: And for alliance’ sake, declare the cause

lines.speaker: PLANTAGENET
lines.text: My father, Earl of Cambridge, lost his head.

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: That cause, fair nephew, that imprison’d me

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: And hath detain’d me all my flowering youth

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: Within a loathsome dungeon, there to pine,

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: Was cursed instrument of his decease.

lines.speaker: PLANTAGENET
lines.text: Discover more at large what cause that was,

lines.speaker: PLANTAGENET
lines.text: For I am ignorant and cannot guess.

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: I will, if that my fading breath permit

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: And death approach not ere my tale be done.

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: Henry the Fourth, grandfather to this king,

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: Deposed his nephew Richard, Edward’s son,

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: The first-begotten and the lawful heir

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: Of Edward king, the third of that descent;

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: During whose reign the Percies of the north,

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: Finding his usurpation most unjust,

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: Endeavour’d my advancement to the throne.

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: The reason moved these warlike lords to this

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: Was, for that—young King Richard thus removed,

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: Leaving no heir begotten of his body—

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: I was the next by birth and parentage;

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: For by my mother I derived am

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: From Lionel Duke of Clarence, third son

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: To King Edward the Third; whereas he

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: From John of Gaunt doth bring his pedigree,

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: Being but fourth of that heroic line.

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: But mark: as in this haughty great attempt

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: They labored to plant the rightful heir,

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: I lost my liberty and they their lives.

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: Long after this, when Henry the Fifth,

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: Succeeding his father Bolingbroke, did reign,

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: Thy father, Earl of Cambridge then, derived

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: From famous Edmund Langley, Duke of York,

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: Marrying my sister that thy mother was,

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: Again, in pity of my hard distress.

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: Levied an army, weening to redeem

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: And have install’d me in the diadem.

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: But, as the rest, so fell that noble earl

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: And was beheaded. Thus the Mortimers,

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: In whom the title rested, were suppress’d.

lines.speaker: PLANTAGENET
lines.text: Of which, my lord, your honour is the last.

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: True; and thou seest that I no issue have,

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: And that my fainting words do warrant death.

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: Thou art my heir; the rest I wish thee gather.

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: But yet be wary in thy studious care.

lines.speaker: PLANTAGENET
lines.text: Thy grave admonishments prevail with me.

lines.speaker: PLANTAGENET
lines.text: But yet methinks, my father’s execution

lines.speaker: PLANTAGENET
lines.text: Was nothing less than bloody tyranny.

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: With silence, nephew, be thou politic;

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: Strong-fixed is the house of Lancaster,

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: And like a mountain, not to be removed.

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: But now thy uncle is removing hence,

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: As princes do their courts when they are cloy’d

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: With long continuance in a settled place.

lines.speaker: PLANTAGENET
lines.text: O uncle, would some part of my young years

lines.speaker: PLANTAGENET
lines.text: Might but redeem the passage of your age!

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: Thou dost then wrong me, as that slaughterer doth

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: Which giveth many wounds when one will kill.

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: Mourn not, except thou sorrow for my good;

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: Only give order for my funeral.

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: And so farewell, and fair be all thy hopes,

lines.speaker: MORTIMER
lines.text: And prosperous be thy life in peace and war!
[_Dies._]

lines.speaker: PLANTAGENET
lines.text: And peace, no war, befall thy parting soul!

lines.speaker: PLANTAGENET
lines.text: In prison hast thou spent a pilgrimage,

lines.speaker: PLANTAGENET
lines.text: And like a hermit overpass’d thy days.

lines.speaker: PLANTAGENET
lines.text: Well, I will lock his counsel in my breast;

lines.speaker: PLANTAGENET
lines.text: And what I do imagine, let that rest.

lines.speaker: PLANTAGENET
lines.text: Keepers, convey him hence; and I myself

lines.speaker: PLANTAGENET
lines.text: Will see his burial better than his life.
[_Exeunt Jailers, bearing out the body of Mortimer._]

lines.speaker: PLANTAGENET
lines.text: Here dies the dusky torch of Mortimer,

lines.speaker: PLANTAGENET
lines.text: Choked with ambition of the meaner sort.

lines.speaker: PLANTAGENET
lines.text: And for those wrongs, those bitter injuries,

lines.speaker: PLANTAGENET
lines.text: Which Somerset hath offer’d to my house,

lines.speaker: PLANTAGENET
lines.text: I doubt not but with honour to redress;

lines.speaker: PLANTAGENET
lines.text: And therefore haste I to the Parliament,

lines.speaker: PLANTAGENET
lines.text: Either to be restored to my blood,

lines.speaker: PLANTAGENET
lines.text: Or make mine ill th’ advantage of my good.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: WINCHESTER
lines.text: Com’st thou with deep premeditated lines,

lines.speaker: WINCHESTER
lines.text: With written pamphlets studiously devised,

lines.speaker: WINCHESTER
lines.text: Humphrey of Gloucester? If thou canst accuse

lines.speaker: WINCHESTER
lines.text: Or aught intend’st to lay unto my charge,

lines.speaker: WINCHESTER
lines.text: Do it without invention, suddenly;

lines.speaker: WINCHESTER
lines.text: As I with sudden and extemporal speech

lines.speaker: WINCHESTER
lines.text: Purpose to answer what thou canst object.
