lines.text: Presumptuous priest, this place commands my patience,

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Or thou shouldst find thou hast dishonour’d me.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Think not, although in writing I preferr’d

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: The manner of thy vile outrageous crimes,

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: That therefore I have forged, or am not able

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Verbatim to rehearse the method of my pen.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: No, prelate; such is thy audacious wickedness,

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Thy lewd, pestiferous, and dissentious pranks,

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: As very infants prattle of thy pride.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Thou art a most pernicious usurer,

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Froward by nature, enemy to peace;

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Lascivious, wanton, more than well beseems

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: A man of thy profession and degree;

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: And for thy treachery, what’s more manifest,

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: In that thou laid’st a trap to take my life,

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: As well at London Bridge as at the Tower?

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Beside, I fear me, if thy thoughts are sifted,

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: The King, thy sovereign, is not quite exempt

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: From envious malice of thy swelling heart.

lines.speaker: WINCHESTER
lines.text: Gloucester, I do defy thee. Lords, vouchsafe

lines.speaker: WINCHESTER
lines.text: To give me hearing what I shall reply.

lines.speaker: WINCHESTER
lines.text: If I were covetous, ambitious, or perverse,

lines.speaker: WINCHESTER
lines.text: As he will have me, how am I so poor?

lines.speaker: WINCHESTER
lines.text: Or how haps it I seek not to advance

lines.speaker: WINCHESTER
lines.text: Or raise myself, but keep my wonted calling?

lines.speaker: WINCHESTER
lines.text: And for dissension, who preferreth peace

lines.speaker: WINCHESTER
lines.text: More than I do, except I be provoked?

lines.speaker: WINCHESTER
lines.text: No, my good lords, it is not that offends;

lines.speaker: WINCHESTER
lines.text: It is not that that hath incensed the Duke.

lines.speaker: WINCHESTER
lines.text: It is because no one should sway but he,

lines.speaker: WINCHESTER
lines.text: No one but he should be about the King;

lines.speaker: WINCHESTER
lines.text: And that engenders thunder in his breast

lines.speaker: WINCHESTER
lines.text: And makes him roar these accusations forth.

lines.speaker: WINCHESTER
lines.text: But he shall know I am as good—

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: As good!

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Thou bastard of my grandfather!

lines.speaker: WINCHESTER
lines.text: Ay, lordly sir; for what are you, I pray,

lines.speaker: WINCHESTER
lines.text: But one imperious in another’s throne?

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Am I not Protector, saucy priest?

lines.speaker: WINCHESTER
lines.text: And am not I a prelate of the church?

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Yes, as an outlaw in a castle keeps,

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: And useth it to patronage his theft.

lines.speaker: WINCHESTER
lines.text: Unreverent Gloucester!

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Thou art reverend

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Touching thy spiritual function, not thy life.

lines.speaker: WINCHESTER
lines.text: Rome shall remedy this.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Roam thither, then.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: My lord, it were your duty to forbear.

lines.speaker: SOMERSET
lines.text: Ay, so the bishop be not overborne.

lines.speaker: SOMERSET
lines.text: Methinks my lord should be religious,

lines.speaker: SOMERSET
lines.text: And know the office that belongs to such.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Methinks his lordship should be humbler;

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: It fitteth not a prelate so to plead.

lines.speaker: SOMERSET
lines.text: Yes, when his holy state is touch’d so near.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: State holy or unhallow’d, what of that?

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Is not his Grace Protector to the King?
[_Aside_.]

lines.speaker: PLANTAGENET
lines.text: Plantagenet, I see, must hold his tongue,

lines.speaker: PLANTAGENET
lines.text: Lest it be said, “Speak, sirrah, when you should;

lines.speaker: PLANTAGENET
lines.text: Must your bold verdict enter talk with lords?”

lines.speaker: PLANTAGENET
lines.text: Else would I have a fling at Winchester.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Uncles of Gloucester and of Winchester,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: The special watchmen of our English weal,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: I would prevail, if prayers might prevail,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: To join your hearts in love and amity.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: O, what a scandal is it to our crown

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: That two such noble peers as ye should jar!

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Believe me, lords, my tender years can tell

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Civil dissension is a viperous worm

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: That gnaws the bowels of the commonwealth.
[_A noise within, “Down with the tawny-coats!”._]

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: What tumult’s this?

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: An uproar, I dare warrant,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Begun through malice of the Bishop’s men.
[_A noise again, “Stones! stones!”_]
Enter Mayor.

lines.speaker: MAYOR
lines.text: O, my good lords, and virtuous Henry,

lines.speaker: MAYOR
lines.text: Pity the city of London, pity us!

lines.speaker: MAYOR
lines.text: The Bishop and the Duke of Gloucester’s men,

lines.speaker: MAYOR
lines.text: Forbidden late to carry any weapon,

lines.speaker: MAYOR
lines.text: Have fill’d their pockets full of pebble stones

lines.speaker: MAYOR
lines.text: And, banding themselves in contrary parts,

lines.speaker: MAYOR
lines.text: Do pelt so fast at one another’s pate

lines.speaker: MAYOR
lines.text: That many have their giddy brains knock’d out;

lines.speaker: MAYOR
lines.text: Our windows are broke down in every street,

lines.speaker: MAYOR
lines.text: And we for fear compell’d to shut our shops.
Enter Servingmen in skirmish with bloody pates.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: We charge you, on allegiance to ourself,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: To hold your slaughtering hands and keep the peace.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Pray, uncle Gloucester, mitigate this strife.

lines.speaker: FIRST SERVINGMAN
lines.text: Nay, if we be forbidden stones, we’ll fall to it with our teeth.

lines.speaker: SECOND SERVINGMAN
lines.text: Do what ye dare, we are as resolute.
[_Skirmish again._]

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: You of my household, leave this peevish broil,

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: And set this unaccustom’d fight aside.

lines.speaker: THIRD SERVINGMAN
lines.text: My lord, we know your Grace to be a man

lines.speaker: THIRD SERVINGMAN
lines.text: Just and upright, and, for your royal birth,

lines.speaker: THIRD SERVINGMAN
lines.text: Inferior to none but to his Majesty;

lines.speaker: THIRD SERVINGMAN
lines.text: And ere that we will suffer such a prince,

lines.speaker: THIRD SERVINGMAN
lines.text: So kind a father of the commonweal,

lines.speaker: THIRD SERVINGMAN
lines.text: To be disgraced by an inkhorn mate,

lines.speaker: THIRD SERVINGMAN
lines.text: We and our wives and children all will fight

lines.speaker: THIRD SERVINGMAN
lines.text: And have our bodies slaughter’d by thy foes.

lines.speaker: FIRST SERVINGMAN
lines.text: Ay, and the very parings of our nails

lines.speaker: FIRST SERVINGMAN
lines.text: Shall pitch a field when we are dead.
[_Begin again._]

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Stay, stay, I say!

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: And if you love me, as you say you do,

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Let me persuade you to forbear awhile.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: O, how this discord doth afflict my soul!

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Can you, my Lord of Winchester, behold

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: My sighs and tears, and will not once relent?

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Who should be pitiful, if you be not?

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Or who should study to prefer a peace

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: If holy churchmen take delight in broils?

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Yield, my Lord Protector; yield, Winchester;

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Except you mean with obstinate repulse

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: To slay your sovereign and destroy the realm.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: You see what mischief and what murder too,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Hath been enacted through your enmity;

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Then be at peace, except ye thirst for blood.

lines.speaker: WINCHESTER
lines.text: He shall submit, or I will never yield.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Compassion on the King commands me stoop,

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Or I would see his heart out, ere the priest

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Should ever get that privilege of me.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Behold, my Lord of Winchester, the Duke

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Hath banish’d moody discontented fury,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: As by his smoothed brows it doth appear.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Why look you still so stern and tragical?

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Here, Winchester, I offer thee my hand.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Fie, uncle Beaufort! I have heard you preach

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: That malice was a great and grievous sin;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And will not you maintain the thing you teach,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: But prove a chief offender in the same?

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Sweet King! The bishop hath a kindly gird.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: For shame, my Lord of Winchester, relent!

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: What, shall a child instruct you what to do?

lines.speaker: WINCHESTER
lines.text: Well, Duke of Gloucester, I will yield to thee;

lines.speaker: WINCHESTER
lines.text: Love for thy love and hand for hand I give.
[_Aside_.]

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Ay, but, I fear me, with a hollow heart.—

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: See here, my friends and loving countrymen,

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: This token serveth for a flag of truce

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Betwixt ourselves and all our followers,

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: So help me God, as I dissemble not!
[_Aside_.]

lines.speaker: WINCHESTER
lines.text: So help me God, as I intend it not!

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: O loving uncle, kind Duke of Gloucester,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: How joyful am I made by this contract!

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Away, my masters, trouble us no more,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: But join in friendship, as your lords have done.

lines.speaker: FIRST SERVINGMAN
lines.text: Content. I’ll to the surgeon’s.

lines.speaker: SECOND SERVINGMAN
lines.text: And so will I.

lines.speaker: THIRD SERVINGMAN
lines.text: And I will see what physic the tavern affords.
[_Exeunt Servingmen, Mayor, &c._]

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Accept this scroll, most gracious sovereign,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Which in the right of Richard Plantagenet

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: We do exhibit to your Majesty.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Well urged, my Lord of Warwick. For, sweet prince,

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: An if your Grace mark every circumstance,

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: You have great reason to do Richard right,

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Especially for those occasions

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: At Eltham Place I told your Majesty.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And those occasions, uncle, were of force;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Therefore, my loving lords, our pleasure is

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: That Richard be restored to his blood.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Let Richard be restored to his blood;

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: So shall his father’s wrongs be recompensed.

lines.speaker: WINCHESTER
lines.text: As will the rest, so willeth Winchester.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: If Richard will be true, not that alone

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: But all the whole inheritance I give

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: That doth belong unto the house of York,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: From whence you spring by lineal descent.

lines.speaker: PLANTAGENET
lines.text: Thy humble servant vows obedience

lines.speaker: PLANTAGENET
lines.text: And humble service till the point of death.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Stoop then and set your knee against my foot;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And in reguerdon of that duty done

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: I girt thee with the valiant sword of York.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Rise, Richard, like a true Plantagenet,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And rise created princely Duke of York.

lines.speaker: PLANTAGENET
lines.text: And so thrive Richard as thy foes may fall!

lines.speaker: PLANTAGENET
lines.text: And as my duty springs, so perish they

lines.speaker: PLANTAGENET
lines.text: That grudge one thought against your Majesty!

lines.speaker: ALL
lines.text: Welcome, high prince, the mighty Duke of York!
[_Aside_.]

lines.speaker: SOMERSET
lines.text: Perish, base prince, ignoble Duke of York!

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Now will it best avail your Majesty

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: To cross the seas and to be crown’d in France.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: The presence of a king engenders love

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Amongst his subjects and his loyal friends,

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: As it disanimates his enemies.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: When Gloucester says the word, King Henry goes;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: For friendly counsel cuts off many foes.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Your ships already are in readiness.
[_Sennet. Flourish. Exeunt all but Exeter._]

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: Ay, we may march in England or in France,

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: Not seeing what is likely to ensue.

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: This late dissension grown betwixt the peers

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: Burns under feigned ashes of forged love,

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: And will at last break out into a flame;

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: As festered members rot but by degree

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: Till bones and flesh and sinews fall away,

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: So will this base and envious discord breed.

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: And now I fear that fatal prophecy

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: Which in the time of Henry named the Fifth

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: Was in the mouth of every sucking babe:

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: That Henry born at Monmouth should win all,

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: And Henry born at Windsor lose all,

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: Which is so plain that Exeter doth wish

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: His days may finish ere that hapless time.
[_Exit._]
Enter La Pucelle with four Soldiers with sacks upon their backs.

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: These are the city gates, the gates of Rouen,

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: Through which our policy must make a breach.

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: Take heed, be wary how you place your words;

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: Talk like the vulgar sort of market men

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: That come to gather money for their corn.

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: If we have entrance, as I hope we shall,

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: And that we find the slothful watch but weak,

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: I’ll by a sign give notice to our friends,

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: That Charles the Dauphin may encounter them.

lines.speaker: FIRST SOLDIER
lines.text: Our sacks shall be a mean to sack the city,

lines.speaker: FIRST SOLDIER
lines.text: And we be lords and rulers over Rouen;

lines.speaker: FIRST SOLDIER
lines.text: Therefore we’ll knock.
[_Knocks._]
[_Within_.]

lines.speaker: WATCH
lines.text: _Qui est la?_

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: _Paysans, la pauvres gens de France:_

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: Poor market folks that come to sell their corn.

lines.speaker: WATCH
lines.text: Enter, go in; the market bell is rung.

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: Now, Rouen, I’ll shake thy bulwarks to the ground.
[_Exeunt._]
Enter Charles, the Bastard of Orleans, Alençon, Reignier and forces.

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: Saint Denis bless this happy stratagem,

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: And once again we’ll sleep secure in Rouen.

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: Here enter’d Pucelle and her practisants;

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: Now she is there, how will she specify

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: Here is the best and safest passage in?

lines.speaker: REIGNIER
lines.text: By thrusting out a torch from yonder tower,

lines.speaker: REIGNIER
lines.text: Which, once discern’d, shows that her meaning is:

lines.speaker: REIGNIER
lines.text: No way to that, for weakness, which she enter’d.
Enter La Pucelle, on the top, thrusting out a torch burning.

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: Behold, this is the happy wedding torch

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: That joineth Rouen unto her countrymen,

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: But burning fatal to the Talbonites.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: See, noble Charles, the beacon of our friend;

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: The burning torch, in yonder turret stands.

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: Now shine it like a comet of revenge,

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: A prophet to the fall of all our foes!

lines.speaker: REIGNIER
lines.text: Defer no time, delays have dangerous ends;
Enter and cry, “The Dauphin!” presently, And then do execution on the watch.
[_Alarum. Exeunt._]

lines.speaker: REIGNIER
lines.text: An alarum. Enter Talbot in an excursion.

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: France, thou shalt rue this treason with thy tears,

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: If Talbot but survive thy treachery.

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Pucelle, that witch, that damned sorceress,

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Hath wrought this hellish mischief unawares,

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: That hardly we escaped the pride of France.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: An alarum. Excursions. Bedford, brought in sick in a chair. Enter

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Talbot and Burgundy without: within, La Pucelle, Charles, Bastard,

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Alençon, and Reignier on the walls.

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: Good morrow, gallants! Want ye corn for bread?

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: I think the Duke of Burgundy will fast

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: Before he’ll buy again at such a rate.

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: ’Twas full of darnel. Do you like the taste?

lines.speaker: BURGUNDY
lines.text: Scoff on, vile fiend and shameless courtezan!

lines.speaker: BURGUNDY
lines.text: I trust ere long to choke thee with thine own,

lines.speaker: BURGUNDY
lines.text: And make thee curse the harvest of that corn.

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: Your Grace may starve, perhaps, before that time.

lines.speaker: BEDFORD
lines.text: O, let no words, but deeds, revenge this treason!

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: What will you do, good graybeard? Break a lance

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: And run a tilt at Death within a chair?

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Foul fiend of France and hag of all despite,

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Encompass’d with thy lustful paramours,

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Becomes it thee to taunt his valiant age

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: And twit with cowardice a man half dead?

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Damsel, I’ll have a bout with you again,

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Or else let Talbot perish with this shame.

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: Are ye so hot? Yet, Pucelle, hold thy peace;

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: If Talbot do but thunder, rain will follow.
[_The English whisper together in council._]

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: God speed the Parliament! Who shall be the Speaker?

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Dare ye come forth and meet us in the field?

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: Belike your lordship takes us then for fools,

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: To try if that our own be ours or no.

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: I speak not to that railing Hecate,

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: But unto thee, Alençon, and the rest;

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Will ye, like soldiers, come and fight it out?

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: ALENÇON.

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Seignieur, no.

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Seignieur, hang! Base muleteers of France!

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Like peasant foot-boys do they keep the walls,

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: And dare not take up arms like gentlemen.

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: Away, captains! Let’s get us from the walls,

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: For Talbot means no goodness by his looks.

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: Goodbye, my lord; we came but to tell you

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: That we are here.
[_Exeunt from the walls._]

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: And there will we be too, ere it be long,

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Or else reproach be Talbot’s greatest fame!

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Vow, Burgundy, by honour of thy house,

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Prick’d on by public wrongs sustain’d in France,

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Either to get the town again or die.

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: And I, as sure as English Henry lives,

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: And as his father here was conqueror,

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: As sure as in this late-betrayed town

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Great Coeur-de-lion’s heart was buried,

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: So sure I swear to get the town or die.

lines.speaker: BURGUNDY
lines.text: My vows are equal partners with thy vows.

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: But, ere we go, regard this dying prince,

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: The valiant Duke of Bedford. Come, my lord,

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: We will bestow you in some better place,

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Fitter for sickness and for crazy age.

lines.speaker: BEDFORD
lines.text: Lord Talbot, do not so dishonour me.

lines.speaker: BEDFORD
lines.text: Here will I sit before the walls of Rouen,

lines.speaker: BEDFORD
lines.text: And will be partner of your weal or woe.

lines.speaker: BURGUNDY
lines.text: Courageous Bedford, let us now persuade you.

lines.speaker: BEDFORD
lines.text: Not to be gone from hence; for once I read

lines.speaker: BEDFORD
lines.text: That stout Pendragon in his litter sick

lines.speaker: BEDFORD
lines.text: Came to the field and vanquished his foes.

lines.speaker: BEDFORD
lines.text: Methinks I should revive the soldiers’ hearts,

lines.speaker: BEDFORD
lines.text: Because I ever found them as myself.

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Undaunted spirit in a dying breast!

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Then be it so. Heavens keep old Bedford safe!

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: And now no more ado, brave Burgundy,

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: But gather we our forces out of hand

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: And set upon our boasting enemy.
[_Exeunt all but Bedford and Attendants._]

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: An alarum. Excursions. Enter Sir John Fastolf and a Captain.

lines.speaker: CAPTAIN
lines.text: Whither away, Sir John Fastolf, in such haste?

lines.speaker: FASTOLF
lines.text: Whither away? To save myself by flight.

lines.speaker: FASTOLF
lines.text: We are like to have the overthrow again.

lines.speaker: CAPTAIN
lines.text: What! Will you fly, and leave Lord Talbot?

lines.speaker: FASTOLF
lines.text: Ay,

lines.speaker: FASTOLF
lines.text: All the Talbots in the world, to save my life.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: CAPTAIN
lines.text: Cowardly knight, ill fortune follow thee!
[_Exit._]
Retreat. Excursions. La Pucelle, Alençon and Charles fly.

lines.speaker: BEDFORD
lines.text: Now, quiet soul, depart when heaven please,

lines.speaker: BEDFORD
lines.text: For I have seen our enemies’ overthrow.

lines.speaker: BEDFORD
lines.text: What is the trust or strength of foolish man?

lines.speaker: BEDFORD
lines.text: They that of late were daring with their scoffs

lines.speaker: BEDFORD
lines.text: Are glad and fain by flight to save themselves.
[_Bedford dies, and is carried in by two in his chair._]

lines.speaker: BEDFORD
lines.text: An alarum. Enter Talbot, Burgundy and the rest.

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Lost, and recover’d in a day again!

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: This is a double honour, Burgundy.

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Yet heavens have glory for this victory!

lines.speaker: BURGUNDY
lines.text: Warlike and martial Talbot, Burgundy

lines.speaker: BURGUNDY
lines.text: Enshrines thee in his heart, and there erects

lines.speaker: BURGUNDY
lines.text: Thy noble deeds as valour’s monuments.

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Thanks, gentle Duke. But where is Pucelle now?

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: I think her old familiar is asleep.

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Now where’s the Bastard’s braves, and Charles his gleeks?

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: What, all amort? Rouen hangs her head for grief

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: That such a valiant company are fled.

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Now will we take some order in the town,

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Placing therein some expert officers,

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: And then depart to Paris to the King,

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: For there young Henry with his nobles lie.

lines.speaker: BURGUNDY
lines.text: What wills Lord Talbot pleaseth Burgundy.

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: But yet, before we go, let’s not forget

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: The noble Duke of Bedford late deceased,

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: But see his exequies fulfill’d in Rouen.

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: A braver soldier never couched lance,

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: A gentler heart did never sway in court;

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: But kings and mightiest potentates must die,

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: For that’s the end of human misery.
[_Exeunt._]
Enter Charles, the Bastard of Orleans, Alençon, La Pucelle and forces.

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: Dismay not, princes, at this accident,

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: Nor grieve that Rouen is so recovered.

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: Care is no cure, but rather corrosive,

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: For things that are not to be remedied.

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: Let frantic Talbot triumph for a while

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: And like a peacock sweep along his tail;

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: We’ll pull his plumes and take away his train,

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: If Dauphin and the rest will be but ruled.

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: We have been guided by thee hitherto,

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: And of thy cunning had no diffidence.

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: One sudden foil shall never breed distrust

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: Search out thy wit for secret policies,

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: And we will make thee famous through the world.

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: ALENÇON.

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: We’ll set thy statue in some holy place,

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: And have thee reverenced like a blessed saint.

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: Employ thee then, sweet virgin, for our good.

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: Then thus it must be; this doth Joan devise:

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: By fair persuasions mix’d with sugar’d words

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: We will entice the Duke of Burgundy

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: To leave the Talbot and to follow us.

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: Ay, marry, sweeting, if we could do that,

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: France were no place for Henry’s warriors;

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: Nor should that nation boast it so with us,

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: But be extirped from our provinces.

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: ALENÇON.

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: For ever should they be expulsed from France,

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: And not have title of an earldom here.

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: Your honours shall perceive how I will work

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: To bring this matter to the wished end.
[_Drum sounds afar off._]

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: Hark! By the sound of drum you may perceive

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: Their powers are marching unto Paris-ward.
[_Here sound an English march._]

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: There goes the Talbot, with his colours spread,

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: And all the troops of English after him.
[_French march._]

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: Now in the rearward comes the Duke and his.

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: Fortune in favour makes him lag behind.

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: Summon a parley; we will talk with him.
[_Trumpets sound a parley._]

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: A parley with the Duke of Burgundy!
Enter Burgundy.

lines.speaker: BURGUNDY
lines.text: Who craves a parley with the Burgundy?

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: The princely Charles of France, thy countryman.

lines.speaker: BURGUNDY
lines.text: What say’st thou, Charles? for I am marching hence.

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: Speak, Pucelle, and enchant him with thy words.

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: Brave Burgundy, undoubted hope of France,

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: Stay, let thy humble handmaid speak to thee.

lines.speaker: BURGUNDY
lines.text: Speak on, but be not over-tedious.

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: Look on thy country, look on fertile France,

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: And see the cities and the towns defaced

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: By wasting ruin of the cruel foe.

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: As looks the mother on her lowly babe

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: When death doth close his tender dying eyes,

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: See, see the pining malady of France;

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: Behold the wounds, the most unnatural wounds,

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: Which thou thyself hast given her woeful breast.

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: O, turn thy edged sword another way;

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: Strike those that hurt, and hurt not those that help.

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: One drop of blood drawn from thy country’s bosom

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: Should grieve thee more than streams of foreign gore.

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: Return thee therefore with a flood of tears,

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: And wash away thy country’s stained spots.

lines.speaker: BURGUNDY
lines.text: Either she hath bewitch’d me with her words,

lines.speaker: BURGUNDY
lines.text: Or nature makes me suddenly relent.

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: Besides, all French and France exclaims on thee,

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: Doubting thy birth and lawful progeny.

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: Who join’st thou with but with a lordly nation

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: That will not trust thee but for profit’s sake?

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: When Talbot hath set footing once in France,

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: And fashion’d thee that instrument of ill,

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: Who then but English Henry will be lord,

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: And thou be thrust out like a fugitive?

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: Call we to mind, and mark but this for proof:

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: Was not the Duke of Orleans thy foe?

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: And was he not in England prisoner?

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: But when they heard he was thine enemy,

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: They set him free without his ransom paid,

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: In spite of Burgundy and all his friends.

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: See then, thou fight’st against thy countrymen,

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: And join’st with them will be thy slaughtermen.

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: Come, come, return; return, thou wandering lord;

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: Charles and the rest will take thee in their arms.

lines.speaker: BURGUNDY
lines.text: I am vanquished; these haughty words of hers

lines.speaker: BURGUNDY
lines.text: Have batter’d me like roaring cannon-shot,

lines.speaker: BURGUNDY
lines.text: And made me almost yield upon my knees.

lines.speaker: BURGUNDY
lines.text: Forgive me, country, and sweet countrymen!

lines.speaker: BURGUNDY
lines.text: And, lords, accept this hearty kind embrace.

lines.speaker: BURGUNDY
lines.text: My forces and my power of men are yours.

lines.speaker: BURGUNDY
lines.text: So, farewell, Talbot; I’ll no longer trust thee.
[_Aside_.]

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: Done like a Frenchman: turn and turn again.

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: Welcome, brave Duke! Thy friendship makes us fresh.

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: And doth beget new courage in our breasts.

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: ALENÇON.

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: Pucelle hath bravely play’d her part in this,

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: And doth deserve a coronet of gold.

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: Now let us on, my lords, and join our powers,

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: And seek how we may prejudice the foe.
[_Exeunt._]
Enter the King, Gloucester, Bishop of Winchester, Exeter, York, Warwick and Vernon; Suffolk, Somerset, Basset and others. To them, with his soldiers, Talbot.

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: My gracious Prince, and honourable peers,

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Hearing of your arrival in this realm,

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: I have awhile given truce unto my wars

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: To do my duty to my sovereign;

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: In sign whereof, this arm, that hath reclaim’d

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: To your obedience fifty fortresses,

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Twelve cities and seven walled towns of strength,

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Beside five hundred prisoners of esteem,

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Lets fall his sword before your Highness’ feet,

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: And with submissive loyalty of heart

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Ascribes the glory of his conquest got

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: First to my God, and next unto your Grace.
[_Kneels_.]

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Is this the Lord Talbot, uncle Gloucester,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: That hath so long been resident in France?

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Yes, if it please your Majesty, my liege.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Welcome, brave captain and victorious lord!

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: When I was young, as yet I am not old,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: I do remember how my father said

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: A stouter champion never handled sword.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Long since we were resolved of your truth,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Your faithful service, and your toil in war;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Yet never have you tasted our reward,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Or been reguerdon’d with so much as thanks.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Because till now we never saw your face.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Therefore, stand up; and for these good deserts

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: We here create you Earl of Shrewsbury;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And in our coronation take your place.
[_Sennet. Flourish. Exeunt all but Vernon and Basset._]

lines.speaker: VERNON
lines.text: Now, sir, to you that were so hot at sea,

lines.speaker: VERNON
lines.text: Disgracing of these colours that I wear

lines.speaker: VERNON
lines.text: In honour of my noble Lord of York,

lines.speaker: VERNON
lines.text: Dar’st thou maintain the former words thou spak’st?

lines.speaker: BASSET
lines.text: Yes, sir, as well as you dare patronage

lines.speaker: BASSET
lines.text: The envious barking of your saucy tongue

lines.speaker: BASSET
lines.text: Against my lord the Duke of Somerset.

lines.speaker: VERNON
lines.text: Sirrah, thy lord I honour as he is.

lines.speaker: BASSET
lines.text: Why, what is he? As good a man as York.

lines.speaker: VERNON
lines.text: Hark ye; not so: in witness, take ye that.
[_Strikes him._]

lines.speaker: BASSET
lines.text: Villain, thou knowest the law of arms is such

lines.speaker: BASSET
lines.text: That whoso draws a sword, ’tis present death,

lines.speaker: BASSET
lines.text: Or else this blow should broach thy dearest blood.

lines.speaker: BASSET
lines.text: But I’ll unto his Majesty, and crave

lines.speaker: BASSET
lines.text: I may have liberty to venge this wrong;

lines.speaker: BASSET
lines.text: When thou shalt see I’ll meet thee to thy cost.

lines.speaker: VERNON
lines.text: Well, miscreant, I’ll be there as soon as you;

lines.speaker: VERNON
lines.text: And, after, meet you sooner than you would.
[_Exeunt._]
Enter the King, Gloucester, Bishop of Winchester, Talbot, Exeter, York, and Warwick; Suffolk, Somerset, the Governor of Paris, and others.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Lord bishop, set the crown upon his head.

lines.speaker: WINCHESTER
lines.text: God save King Henry, of that name the Sixth!

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Now, Governor of Paris, take your oath,

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: That you elect no other king but him;

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Esteem none friends but such as are his friends,

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: And none your foes but such as shall pretend

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Malicious practices against his state:

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: This shall ye do, so help you righteous God!
Enter Sir John Fastolf.

lines.speaker: FASTOLF
lines.text: My gracious sovereign, as I rode from Calais,

lines.speaker: FASTOLF
lines.text: To haste unto your coronation,

lines.speaker: FASTOLF
lines.text: A letter was deliver’d to my hands,

lines.speaker: FASTOLF
lines.text: Writ to your Grace from th’ Duke of Burgundy.

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Shame to the Duke of Burgundy and thee!

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: I vow’d, base knight, when I did meet thee next,

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: To tear the Garter from thy craven’s leg,
[_Plucking it off_.]

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Which I have done, because unworthily

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Thou wast installed in that high degree.

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Pardon me, princely Henry, and the rest.

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: This dastard, at the battle of Patay,

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: When but in all I was six thousand strong

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: And that the French were almost ten to one,

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Before we met or that a stroke was given,

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Like to a trusty squire did run away;

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: In which assault we lost twelve hundred men;

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Myself and divers gentlemen beside

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Were there surprised and taken prisoners.

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Then judge, great lords, if I have done amiss,

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Or whether that such cowards ought to wear

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: This ornament of knighthood, yea or no?

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: To say the truth, this fact was infamous

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: And ill beseeming any common man,

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Much more a knight, a captain, and a leader.

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: When first this Order was ordain’d, my lords,

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Knights of the Garter were of noble birth,

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Valiant and virtuous, full of haughty courage,

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Such as were grown to credit by the wars;

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Not fearing death nor shrinking for distress,

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: But always resolute in most extremes.

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: He then that is not furnish’d in this sort

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Doth but usurp the sacred name of knight,

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Profaning this most honourable Order,

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: And should, if I were worthy to be judge,

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Be quite degraded, like a hedge-born swain

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: That doth presume to boast of gentle blood.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Stain to thy countrymen, thou hear’st thy doom!

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Be packing, therefore, thou that wast a knight;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Henceforth we banish thee on pain of death.
[_Exit Fastolf._]

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And now, my Lord Protector, view the letter

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Sent from our uncle, Duke of Burgundy.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: What means his Grace, that he hath changed his style?

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: No more but, plain and bluntly, “To the King”!

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Hath he forgot he is his sovereign?

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Or doth this churlish superscription

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Pretend some alteration in good will?

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: What’s here? [_Reads_] “I have, upon especial cause,

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Moved with compassion of my country’s wrack,

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Together with the pitiful complaints

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Of such as your oppression feeds upon,

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Forsaken your pernicious faction

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: And join’d with Charles, the rightful King of France.”

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: O monstrous treachery! Can this be so,

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: That in alliance, amity, and oaths,

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: There should be found such false dissembling guile?

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: What! Doth my uncle Burgundy revolt?

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: He doth, my lord, and is become your foe.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Is that the worst this letter doth contain?

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: It is the worst, and all, my lord, he writes.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Why, then, Lord Talbot there shall talk with him

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And give him chastisement for this abuse.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: How say you, my lord, are you not content?

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Content, my liege! Yes, but that I am prevented,

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: I should have begg’d I might have been employ’d.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Then gather strength and march unto him straight;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Let him perceive how ill we brook his treason,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And what offence it is to flout his friends.

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: I go, my lord, in heart desiring still

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: You may behold confusion of your foes.
[_Exit._]
Enter Vernon and Basset.

lines.speaker: VERNON
lines.text: Grant me the combat, gracious sovereign.

lines.speaker: BASSET
lines.text: And me, my lord, grant me the combat too.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: This is my servant; hear him, noble prince.

lines.speaker: SOMERSET
lines.text: And this is mine, sweet Henry, favour him.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Be patient, lords, and give them leave to speak.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Say, gentlemen, what makes you thus exclaim,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And wherefore crave you combat, or with whom?

lines.speaker: VERNON
lines.text: With him, my lord, for he hath done me wrong.

lines.speaker: BASSET
lines.text: And I with him, for he hath done me wrong.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: What is that wrong whereof you both complain?

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: First let me know, and then I’ll answer you.

lines.speaker: BASSET
lines.text: Crossing the sea from England into France,

lines.speaker: BASSET
lines.text: This fellow here, with envious carping tongue,

lines.speaker: BASSET
lines.text: Upbraided me about the rose I wear,

lines.speaker: BASSET
lines.text: Saying the sanguine colour of the leaves

lines.speaker: BASSET
lines.text: Did represent my master’s blushing cheeks

lines.speaker: BASSET
lines.text: When stubbornly he did repugn the truth

lines.speaker: BASSET
lines.text: About a certain question in the law

lines.speaker: BASSET
lines.text: Argued betwixt the Duke of York and him;

lines.speaker: BASSET
lines.text: With other vile and ignominious terms.

lines.speaker: BASSET
lines.text: In confutation of which rude reproach,

lines.speaker: BASSET
lines.text: And in defence of my lord’s worthiness,

lines.speaker: BASSET
lines.text: I crave the benefit of law of arms.

lines.speaker: VERNON
lines.text: And that is my petition, noble lord;

lines.speaker: VERNON
lines.text: For though he seem with forged quaint conceit

lines.speaker: VERNON
lines.text: To set a gloss upon his bold intent,

lines.speaker: VERNON
lines.text: Yet know, my lord, I was provoked by him,

lines.speaker: VERNON
lines.text: And he first took exceptions at this badge,

lines.speaker: VERNON
lines.text: Pronouncing that the paleness of this flower

lines.speaker: VERNON
lines.text: Bewray’d the faintness of my master’s heart.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Will not this malice, Somerset, be left?

lines.speaker: SOMERSET
lines.text: Your private grudge, my Lord of York, will out,

lines.speaker: SOMERSET
lines.text: Though ne’er so cunningly you smother it.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Good Lord, what madness rules in brainsick men,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: When for so slight and frivolous a cause

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Such factious emulations shall arise!

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Good cousins both, of York and Somerset,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Quiet yourselves, I pray, and be at peace.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Let this dissension first be tried by fight,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: And then your Highness shall command a peace.

lines.speaker: SOMERSET
lines.text: The quarrel toucheth none but us alone;

lines.speaker: SOMERSET
lines.text: Betwixt ourselves let us decide it then.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: There is my pledge; accept it, Somerset.

lines.speaker: VERNON
lines.text: Nay, let it rest where it began at first.

lines.speaker: BASSET
lines.text: Confirm it so, mine honourable lord.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Confirm it so! Confounded be your strife!

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: And perish ye, with your audacious prate!

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Presumptuous vassals, are you not ashamed

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: With this immodest clamorous outrage

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: To trouble and disturb the King and us?

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: And you, my lords, methinks you do not well

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: To bear with their perverse objections,

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Much less to take occasion from their mouths

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: To raise a mutiny betwixt yourselves.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Let me persuade you take a better course.

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: It grieves his Highness. Good my lords, be friends.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Come hither, you that would be combatants:

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Henceforth I charge you, as you love our favour,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Quite to forget this quarrel and the cause.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And you, my lords, remember where we are:

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: In France, amongst a fickle wavering nation;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: If they perceive dissension in our looks,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And that within ourselves we disagree,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: How will their grudging stomachs be provoked

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: To willful disobedience, and rebel!

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Beside, what infamy will there arise

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: When foreign princes shall be certified

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: That for a toy, a thing of no regard,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: King Henry’s peers and chief nobility

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Destroy’d themselves and lost the realm of France!

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: O, think upon the conquest of my father,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: My tender years, and let us not forgo

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: That for a trifle that was bought with blood!

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Let me be umpire in this doubtful strife.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: I see no reason if I wear this rose,
[_Putting on a red rose._]

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: That anyone should therefore be suspicious

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: I more incline to Somerset than York.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Both are my kinsmen, and I love them both.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: As well they may upbraid me with my crown

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Because, forsooth, the King of Scots is crown’d.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: But your discretions better can persuade

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Than I am able to instruct or teach;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And therefore, as we hither came in peace,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: So let us still continue peace and love.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Cousin of York, we institute your Grace

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: To be our Regent in these parts of France;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And, good my Lord of Somerset, unite

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Your troops of horsemen with his bands of foot;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And like true subjects, sons of your progenitors,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Go cheerfully together and digest

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Your angry choler on your enemies.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Ourself, my Lord Protector, and the rest

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: After some respite will return to Calais;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: From thence to England, where I hope ere long

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: To be presented, by your victories,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: With Charles, Alençon, and that traitorous rout.
[_Flourish. Exeunt all but York, Warwick, Exeter and Vernon._]

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: My Lord of York, I promise you the King

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Prettily, methought, did play the orator.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: And so he did; but yet I like it not,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: In that he wears the badge of Somerset.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Tush, that was but his fancy; blame him not;

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: I dare presume, sweet prince, he thought no harm.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: An if I wist he did—but let it rest;

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Other affairs must now be managed.
[_Exeunt all but Exeter._]

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: Well didst thou, Richard, to suppress thy voice;

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: For, had the passions of thy heart burst out,

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: I fear we should have seen decipher’d there

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: More rancorous spite, more furious raging broils,

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: Than yet can be imagined or supposed.

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: But howsoe’er, no simple man that sees

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: This jarring discord of nobility,

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: This shouldering of each other in the court,

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: This factious bandying of their favourites,

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: But sees it doth presage some ill event.

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: ’Tis much when scepters are in children’s hands;

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: But more when envy breeds unkind division:

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: There comes the ruin, there begins confusion.
[_Exit._]
Enter Talbot with trump and drum.

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Go to the gates of Bordeaux, trumpeter.

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Summon their general unto the wall.

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Trumpet sounds. Enter  General and others aloft.

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: English John Talbot, captains, calls you forth,

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Servant in arms to Harry King of England;

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: And thus he would: Open your city gates,

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Be humble to us, call my sovereign yours,

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: And do him homage as obedient subjects,

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: And I’ll withdraw me and my bloody power.

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: But if you frown upon this proffer’d peace,

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: You tempt the fury of my three attendants,

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Lean Famine, quartering Steel, and climbing Fire,

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Who in a moment even with the earth

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Shall lay your stately and air-braving towers,

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: If you forsake the offer of their love.

lines.speaker: GENERAL
lines.text: Thou ominous and fearful owl of death,

lines.speaker: GENERAL
lines.text: Our nation’s terror and their bloody scourge!

lines.speaker: GENERAL
lines.text: The period of thy tyranny approacheth.

lines.speaker: GENERAL
lines.text: On us thou canst not enter but by death;

lines.speaker: GENERAL
lines.text: For, I protest, we are well fortified

lines.speaker: GENERAL
lines.text: And strong enough to issue out and fight.

lines.speaker: GENERAL
lines.text: If thou retire, the Dauphin, well appointed,

lines.speaker: GENERAL
lines.text: Stands with the snares of war to tangle thee.

lines.speaker: GENERAL
lines.text: On either hand thee there are squadrons pitch’d

lines.speaker: GENERAL
lines.text: To wall thee from the liberty of flight;

lines.speaker: GENERAL
lines.text: And no way canst thou turn thee for redress

lines.speaker: GENERAL
lines.text: But Death doth front thee with apparent spoil,

lines.speaker: GENERAL
lines.text: And pale Destruction meets thee in the face.

lines.speaker: GENERAL
lines.text: Ten thousand French have ta’en the sacrament

lines.speaker: GENERAL
lines.text: To rive their dangerous artillery

lines.speaker: GENERAL
lines.text: Upon no Christian soul but English Talbot.

lines.speaker: GENERAL
lines.text: Lo, there thou stand’st, a breathing valiant man

lines.speaker: GENERAL
lines.text: Of an invincible unconquer’d spirit.

lines.speaker: GENERAL
lines.text: This is the latest glory of thy praise

lines.speaker: GENERAL
lines.text: That I, thy enemy, due thee withal;

lines.speaker: GENERAL
lines.text: For ere the glass, that now begins to run,

lines.speaker: GENERAL
lines.text: Finish the process of his sandy hour,

lines.speaker: GENERAL
lines.text: These eyes, that see thee now well coloured,

lines.speaker: GENERAL
lines.text: Shall see thee wither’d, bloody, pale, and dead.
[_Drum afar off._]

lines.speaker: GENERAL
lines.text: Hark, hark, the Dauphin’s drum, a warning bell,

lines.speaker: GENERAL
lines.text: Sings heavy music to thy timorous soul,

lines.speaker: GENERAL
lines.text: And mine shall ring thy dire departure out.
[_Exeunt General, etc._]

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: He fables not; I hear the enemy.

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Out, some light horsemen, and peruse their wings.

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: O, negligent and heedless discipline!

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: How are we park’d and bounded in a pale,

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: A little herd of England’s timorous deer,

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Mazed with a yelping kennel of French curs!

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: If we be English deer, be then in blood;

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Not rascal-like, to fall down with a pinch,

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: But rather, moody-mad and desperate stags,

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Turn on the bloody hounds with heads of steel

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: And make the cowards stand aloof at bay.

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Sell every man his life as dear as mine,

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: And they shall find dear deer of us, my friends.

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: God and Saint George, Talbot and England’s right,

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Prosper our colours in this dangerous fight!
[_Exeunt._]
Enter a Messenger that meets York. Enter York with trumpet and many soldiers

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Are not the speedy scouts return’d again

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: That dogg’d the mighty army of the Dauphin?

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: They are return’d, my lord, and give it out

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: That he is march’d to Bordeaux with his power,

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: To fight with Talbot. As he march’d along,

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: By your espials were discovered

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: Two mightier troops than that the Dauphin led,

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: Which join’d with him and made their march for Bordeaux.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: A plague upon that villain Somerset

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: That thus delays my promised supply

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Of horsemen that were levied for this siege!

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Renowned Talbot doth expect my aid,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: And I am louted by a traitor villain

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: And cannot help the noble chevalier.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: God comfort him in this necessity!

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: If he miscarry, farewell wars in France.
Enter Sir William Lucy.

lines.speaker: LUCY
lines.text: Thou princely leader of our English strength,

lines.speaker: LUCY
lines.text: Never so needful on the earth of France,

lines.speaker: LUCY
lines.text: Spur to the rescue of the noble Talbot,

lines.speaker: LUCY
lines.text: Who now is girdled with a waist of iron,

lines.speaker: LUCY
lines.text: And hemm’d about with grim destruction.

lines.speaker: LUCY
lines.text: To Bordeaux, warlike Duke! To Bordeaux, York!

lines.speaker: LUCY
lines.text: Else farewell, Talbot, France, and England’s honour.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: O God, that Somerset, who in proud heart

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Doth stop my cornets, were in Talbot’s place!

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: So should we save a valiant gentleman

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: By forfeiting a traitor and a coward.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Mad ire and wrathful fury makes me weep

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: That thus we die while remiss traitors sleep.

lines.speaker: LUCY
lines.text: O, send some succour to the distress’d lord!

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: He dies, we lose; I break my warlike word;

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: We mourn, France smiles; we lose, they daily get,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: All long of this vile traitor Somerset.

lines.speaker: LUCY
lines.text: Then God take mercy on brave Talbot’s soul,

lines.speaker: LUCY
lines.text: And on his son young John, who two hours since

lines.speaker: LUCY
lines.text: I met in travel toward his warlike father.

lines.speaker: LUCY
lines.text: This seven years did not Talbot see his son;

lines.speaker: LUCY
lines.text: And now they meet where both their lives are done.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Alas, what joy shall noble Talbot have

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: To bid his young son welcome to his grave?

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Away! Vexation almost stops my breath,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: That sunder’d friends greet in the hour of death.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Lucy, farewell. No more my fortune can

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: But curse the cause I cannot aid the man.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Maine, Blois, Poictiers, and Tours, are won away,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Long all of Somerset and his delay.
[_Exit, with his soldiers._]

lines.speaker: LUCY
lines.text: Thus, while the vulture of sedition

lines.speaker: LUCY
lines.text: Feeds in the bosom of such great commanders,

lines.speaker: LUCY
lines.text: Sleeping neglection doth betray to loss

lines.speaker: LUCY
lines.text: The conquest of our scarce-cold conqueror,

lines.speaker: LUCY
lines.text: That ever-living man of memory,

lines.speaker: LUCY
lines.text: Henry the Fifth. Whiles they each other cross,

lines.speaker: LUCY
lines.text: Lives, honours, lands, and all hurry to loss.
[_Exit._]
Enter Somerset with his army; a Captain of Talbot’s with him.

lines.speaker: SOMERSET
lines.text: It is too late; I cannot send them now.

lines.speaker: SOMERSET
lines.text: This expedition was by York and Talbot

lines.speaker: SOMERSET
lines.text: Too rashly plotted. All our general force

lines.speaker: SOMERSET
lines.text: Might with a sally of the very town

lines.speaker: SOMERSET
lines.text: Be buckled with. The over-daring Talbot

lines.speaker: SOMERSET
lines.text: Hath sullied all his gloss of former honour

lines.speaker: SOMERSET
lines.text: By this unheedful, desperate, wild adventure.

lines.speaker: SOMERSET
lines.text: York set him on to fight and die in shame

lines.speaker: SOMERSET
lines.text: That, Talbot dead, great York might bear the name.

lines.speaker: CAPTAIN
lines.text: Here is Sir William Lucy, who with me

lines.speaker: CAPTAIN
lines.text: Set from our o’er-match’d forces forth for aid.
Enter Sir William Lucy.

lines.speaker: SOMERSET
lines.text: How now, Sir William, whither were you sent?

lines.speaker: LUCY
lines.text: Whither, my lord? From bought and sold Lord Talbot,

lines.speaker: LUCY
lines.text: Who, ring’d about with bold adversity,

lines.speaker: LUCY
lines.text: Cries out for noble York and Somerset

lines.speaker: LUCY
lines.text: To beat assailing Death from his weak legions;

lines.speaker: LUCY
lines.text: And whiles the honourable captain there

lines.speaker: LUCY
lines.text: Drops bloody sweat from his war-wearied limbs,

lines.speaker: LUCY
lines.text: And, in advantage lingering, looks for rescue,

lines.speaker: LUCY
lines.text: You, his false hopes, the trust of England’s honour,

lines.speaker: LUCY
lines.text: Keep off aloof with worthless emulation.

lines.speaker: LUCY
lines.text: Let not your private discord keep away

lines.speaker: LUCY
lines.text: The levied succours that should lend him aid,

lines.speaker: LUCY
lines.text: While he, renowned noble gentleman,

lines.speaker: LUCY
lines.text: Yield up his life unto a world of odds.

lines.speaker: LUCY
lines.text: Orleans the Bastard, Charles, Burgundy,

lines.speaker: LUCY
lines.text: Alençon, Reignier, compass him about,

lines.speaker: LUCY
lines.text: And Talbot perisheth by your default.

lines.speaker: SOMERSET
lines.text: York set him on; York should have sent him aid.

lines.speaker: LUCY
lines.text: And York as fast upon your Grace exclaims,

lines.speaker: LUCY
lines.text: Swearing that you withhold his levied host

lines.speaker: LUCY
lines.text: Collected for this expedition.

lines.speaker: SOMERSET
lines.text: York lies; he might have sent and had the horse.

lines.speaker: SOMERSET
lines.text: I owe him little duty, and less love,

lines.speaker: SOMERSET
lines.text: And take foul scorn to fawn on him by sending.

lines.speaker: LUCY
lines.text: The fraud of England, not the force of France,

lines.speaker: LUCY
lines.text: Hath now entrapp’d the noble-minded Talbot.

lines.speaker: LUCY
lines.text: Never to England shall he bear his life,

lines.speaker: LUCY
lines.text: But dies betray’d to fortune by your strife.

lines.speaker: SOMERSET
lines.text: Come, go; I will dispatch the horsemen straight.

lines.speaker: SOMERSET
lines.text: Within six hours they will be at his aid.

lines.speaker: LUCY
lines.text: Too late comes rescue; he is ta’en or slain,

lines.speaker: LUCY
lines.text: For fly he could not if he would have fled;

lines.speaker: LUCY
lines.text: And fly would Talbot never, though he might.

lines.speaker: SOMERSET
lines.text: If he be dead, brave Talbot, then adieu!

lines.speaker: LUCY
lines.text: His fame lives in the world, his shame in you.
[_Exeunt._]
Enter Talbot and John his son.

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: O young John Talbot, I did send for thee

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: To tutor thee in stratagems of war,

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: That Talbot’s name might be in thee revived

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: When sapless age and weak unable limbs

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Should bring thy father to his drooping chair.

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: But—O malignant and ill-boding stars!—

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Now thou art come unto a feast of death,

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: A terrible and unavoided danger.

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Therefore, dear boy, mount on my swiftest horse,

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: And I’ll direct thee how thou shalt escape

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: By sudden flight. Come, dally not, be gone.

lines.speaker: JOHN TALBOT
lines.text: Is my name Talbot? And am I your son?

lines.speaker: JOHN TALBOT
lines.text: And shall I fly? O, if you love my mother,

lines.speaker: JOHN TALBOT
lines.text: Dishonour not her honourable name,

lines.speaker: JOHN TALBOT
lines.text: To make a bastard and a slave of me!

lines.speaker: JOHN TALBOT
lines.text: The world will say, he is not Talbot’s blood,

lines.speaker: JOHN TALBOT
lines.text: That basely fled when noble Talbot stood.

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Fly, to revenge my death if I be slain.

lines.speaker: JOHN TALBOT
lines.text: He that flies so will ne’er return again.

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: If we both stay, we both are sure to die.

lines.speaker: JOHN TALBOT
lines.text: Then let me stay and, father, do you fly.

lines.speaker: JOHN TALBOT
lines.text: Your loss is great, so your regard should be;

lines.speaker: JOHN TALBOT
lines.text: My worth unknown, no loss is known in me.

lines.speaker: JOHN TALBOT
lines.text: Upon my death the French can little boast;

lines.speaker: JOHN TALBOT
lines.text: In yours they will, in you all hopes are lost.

lines.speaker: JOHN TALBOT
lines.text: Flight cannot stain the honour you have won;

lines.speaker: JOHN TALBOT
lines.text: But mine it will, that no exploit have done.

lines.speaker: JOHN TALBOT
lines.text: You fled for vantage, everyone will swear;

lines.speaker: JOHN TALBOT
lines.text: But if I bow, they’ll say it was for fear.

lines.speaker: JOHN TALBOT
lines.text: There is no hope that ever I will stay

lines.speaker: JOHN TALBOT
lines.text: If the first hour I shrink and run away.

lines.speaker: JOHN TALBOT
lines.text: Here on my knee I beg mortality,

lines.speaker: JOHN TALBOT
lines.text: Rather than life preserved with infamy.

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Shall all thy mother’s hopes lie in one tomb?

lines.speaker: JOHN TALBOT
lines.text: Ay, rather than I’ll shame my mother’s womb.

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Upon my blessing, I command thee go.

lines.speaker: JOHN TALBOT
lines.text: To fight I will, but not to fly the foe.

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Part of thy father may be saved in thee.

lines.speaker: JOHN TALBOT
lines.text: No part of him but will be shame in me.

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Thou never hadst renown, nor canst not lose it.

lines.speaker: JOHN TALBOT
lines.text: Yes, your renowned name; shall flight abuse it?

lines.speaker: TALBOT
lines.text: Thy father’s charge shall clear thee from that stain.

lines.speaker: JOHN TALBOT
lines.text: You cannot witness for me, being slain.
