lines.text: A goodly prize, fit for the devil’s grace!

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: See, how the ugly witch doth bend her brows,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: As if with Circe she would change my shape!

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: Chang’d to a worser shape thou canst not be.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: O, Charles the Dauphin is a proper man;

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: No shape but his can please your dainty eye.

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: A plaguing mischief light on Charles and thee!

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: And may ye both be suddenly surprised

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: By bloody hands, in sleeping on your beds!

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Fell banning hag, enchantress, hold thy tongue!

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: I prithee, give me leave to curse awhile.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Curse, miscreant, when thou com’st to the stake.
[_Exeunt._]
Alarum. Enter Suffolk with Margaret in his hand.

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Be what thou wilt, thou art my prisoner.
[_Gazes on her._]

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: O fairest beauty, do not fear nor fly!

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: For I will touch thee but with reverent hands,

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: I kiss these fingers for eternal peace,

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: And lay them gently on thy tender side.

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Who art thou? Say, that I may honour thee.

lines.speaker: MARGARET
lines.text: Margaret my name, and daughter to a king,

lines.speaker: MARGARET
lines.text: The King of Naples, whosoe’er thou art.

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: An earl I am, and Suffolk am I call’d.

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Be not offended, nature’s miracle,

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Thou art allotted to be ta’en by me.

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: So doth the swan her downy cygnets save,

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Keeping them prisoner underneath her wings.

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Yet, if this servile usage once offend,

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Go and be free again as Suffolk’s friend.
[_She is going._]

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: O, stay! I have no power to let her pass;

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: My hand would free her, but my heart says no.

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: As plays the sun upon the glassy streams,

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Twinkling another counterfeited beam,

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: So seems this gorgeous beauty to mine eyes.

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Fain would I woo her, yet I dare not speak.

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: I’ll call for pen and ink, and write my mind.

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Fie, de la Pole, disable not thyself;

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Hast not a tongue? Is she not here?

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Wilt thou be daunted at a woman’s sight?

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Ay, beauty’s princely majesty is such

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Confounds the tongue and makes the senses rough.

lines.speaker: MARGARET
lines.text: Say, Earl of Suffolk, if thy name be so,

lines.speaker: MARGARET
lines.text: What ransom must I pay before I pass?

lines.speaker: MARGARET
lines.text: For I perceive I am thy prisoner.

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: How canst thou tell she will deny thy suit,

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Before thou make a trial of her love?

lines.speaker: MARGARET
lines.text: Why speak’st thou not? What ransom must I pay?

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: She’s beautiful, and therefore to be woo’d;

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: She is a woman, therefore to be won.

lines.speaker: MARGARET
lines.text: Wilt thou accept of ransom, yea, or no?

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Fond man, remember that thou hast a wife;

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Then how can Margaret be thy paramour?

lines.speaker: MARGARET
lines.text: I were best leave him, for he will not hear.

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: There all is marr’d; there lies a cooling card.

lines.speaker: MARGARET
lines.text: He talks at random; sure, the man is mad.

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: And yet a dispensation may be had.

lines.speaker: MARGARET
lines.text: And yet I would that you would answer me.

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: I’ll win this Lady Margaret. For whom?

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Why, for my king. Tush, that’s a wooden thing!

lines.speaker: MARGARET
lines.text: He talks of wood. It is some carpenter.

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Yet so my fancy may be satisfied,

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: And peace established between these realms.

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: But there remains a scruple in that too;

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: For though her father be the King of Naples,

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Duke of Anjou and Maine, yet is he poor,

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: And our nobility will scorn the match.

lines.speaker: MARGARET
lines.text: Hear ye, captain, are you not at leisure?

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: It shall be so, disdain they ne’er so much.

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Henry is youthful and will quickly yield.

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Madam, I have a secret to reveal.

lines.speaker: MARGARET
lines.text: What though I be enthrall’d? He seems a knight,

lines.speaker: MARGARET
lines.text: And will not any way dishonour me.

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Lady, vouchsafe to listen what I say.

lines.speaker: MARGARET
lines.text: Perhaps I shall be rescued by the French;

lines.speaker: MARGARET
lines.text: And then I need not crave his courtesy.

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Sweet madam, give me hearing in a cause.

lines.speaker: MARGARET
lines.text: Tush, women have been captivate ere now.

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Lady, wherefore talk you so?

lines.speaker: MARGARET
lines.text: I cry you mercy, ’tis but _quid_ for _quo_.

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Say, gentle princess, would you not suppose

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Your bondage happy, to be made a queen?

lines.speaker: MARGARET
lines.text: To be a queen in bondage is more vile

lines.speaker: MARGARET
lines.text: Than is a slave in base servility;

lines.speaker: MARGARET
lines.text: For princes should be free.

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: And so shall you,

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: If happy England’s royal king be free.

lines.speaker: MARGARET
lines.text: Why, what concerns his freedom unto me?

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: I’ll undertake to make thee Henry’s queen,

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: To put a golden scepter in thy hand

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: And set a precious crown upon thy head,

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: If thou wilt condescend to be my—

lines.speaker: MARGARET
lines.text: What?

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: His love.

lines.speaker: MARGARET
lines.text: I am unworthy to be Henry’s wife.

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: No, gentle madam, I unworthy am

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: To woo so fair a dame to be his wife,

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: And have no portion in the choice myself.

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: How say you, madam, are ye so content?

lines.speaker: MARGARET
lines.text: An if my father please, I am content.

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Then call our captains and our colours forth.

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: And, madam, at your father’s castle walls

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: We’ll crave a parley, to confer with him.

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: A parley sounded. Enter Reignier on the walls.

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: See, Reignier, see, thy daughter prisoner!

lines.speaker: REIGNIER
lines.text: To whom?

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: To me.

lines.speaker: REIGNIER
lines.text: Suffolk, what remedy?

lines.speaker: REIGNIER
lines.text: I am a soldier, and unapt to weep

lines.speaker: REIGNIER
lines.text: Or to exclaim on fortune’s fickleness.

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Yes, there is remedy enough, my lord:

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Consent, and for thy honour give consent,

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Thy daughter shall be wedded to my king,

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Whom I with pain have woo’d and won thereto;

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: And this her easy-held imprisonment

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Hath gain’d thy daughter princely liberty.

lines.speaker: REIGNIER
lines.text: Speaks Suffolk as he thinks?

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Fair Margaret knows

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: That Suffolk doth not flatter, face, or feign.

lines.speaker: REIGNIER
lines.text: Upon thy princely warrant, I descend

lines.speaker: REIGNIER
lines.text: To give thee answer of thy just demand.
[_Exit from the walls._]

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: And here I will expect thy coming.
Trumpets sound. Enter Reignier, below.

lines.speaker: REIGNIER
lines.text: Welcome, brave earl, into our territories.

lines.speaker: REIGNIER
lines.text: Command in Anjou what your honour pleases.

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Thanks, Reignier, happy for so sweet a child,

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Fit to be made companion with a king.

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: What answer makes your Grace unto my suit?

lines.speaker: REIGNIER
lines.text: Since thou dost deign to woo her little worth

lines.speaker: REIGNIER
lines.text: To be the princely bride of such a lord,

lines.speaker: REIGNIER
lines.text: Upon condition I may quietly

lines.speaker: REIGNIER
lines.text: Enjoy mine own, the country Maine and Anjou,

lines.speaker: REIGNIER
lines.text: Free from oppression or the stroke of war,

lines.speaker: REIGNIER
lines.text: My daughter shall be Henry’s, if he please.

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: That is her ransom; I deliver her;

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: And those two counties I will undertake

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Your Grace shall well and quietly enjoy.

lines.speaker: REIGNIER
lines.text: And I again, in Henry’s royal name,

lines.speaker: REIGNIER
lines.text: As deputy unto that gracious king,

lines.speaker: REIGNIER
lines.text: Give thee her hand for sign of plighted faith.

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Reignier of France, I give thee kingly thanks,

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Because this is in traffic of a king.
[_Aside_.]

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: And yet, methinks, I could be well content

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: To be mine own attorney in this case.

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: I’ll over then to England with this news,

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: And make this marriage to be solemnized.

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: So, farewell, Reignier; set this diamond safe

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: In golden palaces, as it becomes.

lines.speaker: REIGNIER
lines.text: I do embrace thee as I would embrace

lines.speaker: REIGNIER
lines.text: The Christian prince, King Henry, were he here.

lines.speaker: MARGARET
lines.text: Farewell, my lord; good wishes, praise, and prayers

lines.speaker: MARGARET
lines.text: Shall Suffolk ever have of Margaret. [_Going_].

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Farewell, sweet madam; but hark you, Margaret,

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: No princely commendations to my king?

lines.speaker: MARGARET
lines.text: Such commendations as becomes a maid,

lines.speaker: MARGARET
lines.text: A virgin and his servant, say to him.

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Words sweetly placed and modestly directed.

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: But, madam, I must trouble you again:

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: No loving token to his Majesty?

lines.speaker: MARGARET
lines.text: Yes, my good lord; a pure unspotted heart,

lines.speaker: MARGARET
lines.text: Never yet taint with love, I send the King.

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: And this withal.
[_Kisses her_.]

lines.speaker: MARGARET
lines.text: That for thyself. I will not so presume

lines.speaker: MARGARET
lines.text: To send such peevish tokens to a king.
[_Exeunt Reignier and Margaret._]

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: O, wert thou for myself! But, Suffolk, stay;

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Thou mayst not wander in that labyrinth.

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: There Minotaurs and ugly treasons lurk.

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Solicit Henry with her wondrous praise.

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Bethink thee on her virtues that surmount,

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: And natural graces that extinguish art;

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Repeat their semblance often on the seas,

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: That, when thou com’st to kneel at Henry’s feet,

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Thou mayst bereave him of his wits with wonder.
[_Exit._]

scenes.setting: Camp of the Duke of York in Anjou.

lines.text: Enter York, Warwick and others.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Bring forth that sorceress condemn’d to burn.
Enter La Pucelle, guarded, and a Shepherd.

lines.speaker: SHEPHERD
lines.text: Ah, Joan, this kills thy father’s heart outright!

lines.speaker: SHEPHERD
lines.text: Have I sought every country far and near,

lines.speaker: SHEPHERD
lines.text: And, now it is my chance to find thee out,

lines.speaker: SHEPHERD
lines.text: Must I behold thy timeless cruel death?

lines.speaker: SHEPHERD
lines.text: Ah, Joan, sweet daughter Joan, I’ll die with thee!

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: Decrepit miser, base ignoble wretch!

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: I am descended of a gentler blood.

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: Thou art no father nor no friend of mine.

lines.speaker: SHEPHERD
lines.text: Out, out! My lords, as please you, ’tis not so;

lines.speaker: SHEPHERD
lines.text: I did beget her, all the parish knows.

lines.speaker: SHEPHERD
lines.text: Her mother liveth yet, can testify

lines.speaker: SHEPHERD
lines.text: She was the first fruit of my bachelorship.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Graceless, wilt thou deny thy parentage?

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: This argues what her kind of life hath been,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Wicked and vile; and so her death concludes.

lines.speaker: SHEPHERD
lines.text: Fie, Joan, that thou wilt be so obstacle!

lines.speaker: SHEPHERD
lines.text: God knows thou art a collop of my flesh;

lines.speaker: SHEPHERD
lines.text: And for thy sake have I shed many a tear.

lines.speaker: SHEPHERD
lines.text: Deny me not, I prithee, gentle Joan.

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: Peasant, avaunt! You have suborn’d this man

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: Of purpose to obscure my noble birth.

lines.speaker: SHEPHERD
lines.text: ’Tis true, I gave a noble to the priest

lines.speaker: SHEPHERD
lines.text: The morn that I was wedded to her mother.

lines.speaker: SHEPHERD
lines.text: Kneel down and take my blessing, good my girl.

lines.speaker: SHEPHERD
lines.text: Wilt thou not stoop? Now cursed be the time

lines.speaker: SHEPHERD
lines.text: Of thy nativity! I would the milk

lines.speaker: SHEPHERD
lines.text: Thy mother gave thee when thou suck’dst her breast

lines.speaker: SHEPHERD
lines.text: Had been a little ratsbane for thy sake!

lines.speaker: SHEPHERD
lines.text: Or else, when thou didst keep my lambs a-field,

lines.speaker: SHEPHERD
lines.text: I wish some ravenous wolf had eaten thee!

lines.speaker: SHEPHERD
lines.text: Dost thou deny thy father, cursed drab?

lines.speaker: SHEPHERD
lines.text: O, burn her, burn her! Hanging is too good.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Take her away, for she hath lived too long,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: To fill the world with vicious qualities.

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: First, let me tell you whom you have condemn’d:

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: Not one begotten of a shepherd swain,

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: But issued from the progeny of kings;

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: Virtuous and holy, chosen from above,

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: By inspiration of celestial grace,

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: To work exceeding miracles on earth.

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: I never had to do with wicked spirits.

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: But you, that are polluted with your lusts,

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: Stain’d with the guiltless blood of innocents,

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: Corrupt and tainted with a thousand vices,

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: Because you want the grace that others have,

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: You judge it straight a thing impossible

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: To compass wonders but by help of devils.

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: No, misconceived! Joan of Arc hath been

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: A virgin from her tender infancy,

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: Chaste and immaculate in very thought;

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: Whose maiden blood, thus rigorously effused,

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: Will cry for vengeance at the gates of heaven.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Ay, ay; away with her to execution!

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: And hark ye, sirs; because she is a maid,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Spare for no faggots, let there be enow.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Place barrels of pitch upon the fatal stake,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: That so her torture may be shortened.

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: Will nothing turn your unrelenting hearts?

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: Then, Joan, discover thine infirmity,

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: That warranteth by law to be thy privilege:

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: I am with child, ye bloody homicides.

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: Murder not then the fruit within my womb,

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: Although ye hale me to a violent death.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Now heaven forfend! The holy maid with child?

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: The greatest miracle that e’er ye wrought!

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Is all your strict preciseness come to this?

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: She and the Dauphin have been juggling.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: I did imagine what would be her refuge.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Well, go to; we’ll have no bastards live,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Especially since Charles must father it.

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: You are deceived; my child is none of his.

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: It was Alençon that enjoy’d my love.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Alençon, that notorious Machiavel!

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: It dies and if it had a thousand lives.

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: O, give me leave, I have deluded you.

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: ’Twas neither Charles nor yet the Duke I named,

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: But Reignier, King of Naples, that prevail’d.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: A married man! That’s most intolerable.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Why, here’s a girl! I think she knows not well—

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: There were so many—whom she may accuse.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: It’s sign she hath been liberal and free.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: And yet, forsooth, she is a virgin pure!

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Strumpet, thy words condemn thy brat and thee.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Use no entreaty, for it is in vain.

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: Then lead me hence, with whom I leave my curse:

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: May never glorious sun reflex his beams

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: Upon the country where you make abode;

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: But darkness and the gloomy shade of death

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: Environ you, till mischief and despair

lines.speaker: PUCELLE
lines.text: Drive you to break your necks or hang yourselves!
[_Exit, guarded._]

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Break thou in pieces and consume to ashes,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Thou foul accursed minister of hell!
Enter Bishop of Winchester as Cardinal, attended.

lines.speaker: WINCHESTER
lines.text: Lord Regent, I do greet your Excellence

lines.speaker: WINCHESTER
lines.text: With letters of commission from the King.

lines.speaker: WINCHESTER
lines.text: For know, my lords, the states of Christendom,

lines.speaker: WINCHESTER
lines.text: Moved with remorse of these outrageous broils,

lines.speaker: WINCHESTER
lines.text: Have earnestly implored a general peace

lines.speaker: WINCHESTER
lines.text: Betwixt our nation and the aspiring French;

lines.speaker: WINCHESTER
lines.text: And here at hand the Dauphin and his train

lines.speaker: WINCHESTER
lines.text: Approacheth to confer about some matter.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Is all our travail turn’d to this effect?

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: After the slaughter of so many peers,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: So many captains, gentlemen and soldiers,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: That in this quarrel have been overthrown

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: And sold their bodies for their country’s benefit,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Shall we at last conclude effeminate peace?

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Have we not lost most part of all the towns,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: By treason, falsehood, and by treachery,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Our great progenitors had conquered?

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: O, Warwick, Warwick! I foresee with grief

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: The utter loss of all the realm of France.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: Be patient, York; if we conclude a peace,

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: It shall be with such strict and severe covenants

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: As little shall the Frenchmen gain thereby.
Enter Charles, Alençon, Bastard, Reignier and others.

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: Since, lords of England, it is thus agreed

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: That peaceful truce shall be proclaim’d in France,

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: We come to be informed by yourselves

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: What the conditions of that league must be.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Speak, Winchester, for boiling choler chokes

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: The hollow passage of my poison’d voice

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: By sight of these our baleful enemies.

lines.speaker: WINCHESTER
lines.text: Charles, and the rest, it is enacted thus:

lines.speaker: WINCHESTER
lines.text: That, in regard King Henry gives consent,

lines.speaker: WINCHESTER
lines.text: Of mere compassion and of lenity,

lines.speaker: WINCHESTER
lines.text: To ease your country of distressful war,

lines.speaker: WINCHESTER
lines.text: And suffer you to breathe in fruitful peace,

lines.speaker: WINCHESTER
lines.text: You shall become true liegemen to his crown.

lines.speaker: WINCHESTER
lines.text: And, Charles, upon condition thou wilt swear

lines.speaker: WINCHESTER
lines.text: To pay him tribute and submit thyself,

lines.speaker: WINCHESTER
lines.text: Thou shalt be placed as viceroy under him,

lines.speaker: WINCHESTER
lines.text: And still enjoy the regal dignity.

lines.speaker: WINCHESTER
lines.text: ALENÇON.

lines.speaker: WINCHESTER
lines.text: Must he be then as shadow of himself?

lines.speaker: WINCHESTER
lines.text: Adorn his temples with a coronet,

lines.speaker: WINCHESTER
lines.text: And yet, in substance and authority,

lines.speaker: WINCHESTER
lines.text: Retain but privilege of a private man?

lines.speaker: WINCHESTER
lines.text: This proffer is absurd and reasonless.

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: ’Tis known already that I am possess’d

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: With more than half the Gallian territories,

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: And therein reverenced for their lawful king.

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: Shall I, for lucre of the rest unvanquish’d,

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: Detract so much from that prerogative

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: As to be call’d but viceroy of the whole?

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: No, lord ambassador, I’ll rather keep

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: That which I have than, coveting for more,

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: Be cast from possibility of all.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Insulting Charles! Hast thou by secret means

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Used intercession to obtain a league,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: And, now the matter grows to compromise,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Stand’st thou aloof upon comparison?

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Either accept the title thou usurp’st,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Of benefit proceeding from our king

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: And not of any challenge of desert,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Or we will plague thee with incessant wars.

lines.speaker: REIGNIER
lines.text: My lord, you do not well in obstinacy

lines.speaker: REIGNIER
lines.text: To cavil in the course of this contract.

lines.speaker: REIGNIER
lines.text: If once it be neglected, ten to one

lines.speaker: REIGNIER
lines.text: We shall not find like opportunity.

lines.speaker: REIGNIER
lines.text: ALENÇON.

lines.speaker: REIGNIER
lines.text: To say the truth, it is your policy

lines.speaker: REIGNIER
lines.text: To save your subjects from such massacre

lines.speaker: REIGNIER
lines.text: And ruthless slaughters as are daily seen

lines.speaker: REIGNIER
lines.text: By our proceeding in hostility;

lines.speaker: REIGNIER
lines.text: And therefore take this compact of a truce,

lines.speaker: REIGNIER
lines.text: Although you break it when your pleasure serves.

lines.speaker: WARWICK
lines.text: How say’st thou, Charles? Shall our condition stand?

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: It shall; only reserv’d you claim no interest

lines.speaker: CHARLES
lines.text: In any of our towns of garrison.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Then swear allegiance to his Majesty,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: As thou art knight, never to disobey

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Nor be rebellious to the crown of England,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Thou, nor thy nobles, to the crown of England.
[_Charles and the rest give tokens of fealty._]

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: So, now dismiss your army when ye please;

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Hang up your ensigns, let your drums be still,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: For here we entertain a solemn peace.
[_Exeunt._]
Enter Suffolk in conference with the King, Gloucester and Exeter.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Your wondrous rare description, noble earl,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Of beauteous Margaret hath astonish’d me.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Her virtues graced with external gifts

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Do breed love’s settled passions in my heart,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And like as rigor of tempestuous gusts

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Provokes the mightiest hulk against the tide,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: So am I driven by breath of her renown

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Either to suffer shipwreck or arrive

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Where I may have fruition of her love.

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Tush, my good lord, this superficial tale

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Is but a preface of her worthy praise;

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: The chief perfections of that lovely dame,

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Had I sufficient skill to utter them,

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Would make a volume of enticing lines,

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Able to ravish any dull conceit;

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: And, which is more, she is not so divine,

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: So full replete with choice of all delights,

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: But with as humble lowliness of mind

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: She is content to be at your command;

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Command, I mean, of virtuous chaste intents,

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: To love and honour Henry as her lord.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And otherwise will Henry ne’er presume.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Therefore, my Lord Protector, give consent

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: That Margaret may be England’s royal queen.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: So should I give consent to flatter sin.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: You know, my lord, your Highness is betroth’d

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Unto another lady of esteem.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: How shall we then dispense with that contract,

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: And not deface your honour with reproach?

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: As doth a ruler with unlawful oaths;

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Or one that, at a triumph having vow’d

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: To try his strength, forsaketh yet the lists

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: By reason of his adversary’s odds.

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: A poor earl’s daughter is unequal odds,

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: And therefore may be broke without offence.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Why, what, I pray, is Margaret more than that?

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Her father is no better than an earl,

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Although in glorious titles he excel.

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Yes, my lord, her father is a king,

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: The King of Naples and Jerusalem;

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: And of such great authority in France

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: As his alliance will confirm our peace,

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: And keep the Frenchmen in allegiance.

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: And so the Earl of Armagnac may do,

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Because he is near kinsman unto Charles.

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: Beside, his wealth doth warrant a liberal dower,

lines.speaker: EXETER
lines.text: Where Reignier sooner will receive than give.

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: A dower, my lords? Disgrace not so your king,

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: That he should be so abject, base, and poor,

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: To choose for wealth and not for perfect love.

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Henry is able to enrich his queen,

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: And not to seek a queen to make him rich;

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: So worthless peasants bargain for their wives,

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: As market-men for oxen, sheep, or horse.

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Marriage is a matter of more worth

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Than to be dealt in by attorneyship;

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Not whom we will, but whom his Grace affects,

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Must be companion of his nuptial bed.

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: And therefore, lords, since he affects her most,

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Most of all these reasons bindeth us

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: In our opinions she should be preferr’d.

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: For what is wedlock forced but a hell,

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: An age of discord and continual strife?

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Whereas the contrary bringeth bliss,

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: And is a pattern of celestial peace.

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Whom should we match with Henry, being a king,

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: But Margaret, that is daughter to a king?

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Her peerless feature, joined with her birth,

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Approves her fit for none but for a king;

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Her valiant courage and undaunted spirit,

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: More than in women commonly is seen,

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Will answer our hope in issue of a king;

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: For Henry, son unto a conqueror,

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Is likely to beget more conquerors,

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: If with a lady of so high resolve

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: As is fair Margaret he be link’d in love.

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Then yield, my lords; and here conclude with me

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: That Margaret shall be queen, and none but she.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Whether it be through force of your report,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: My noble Lord of Suffolk, or for that

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: My tender youth was never yet attaint

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: With any passion of inflaming love,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: I cannot tell; but this I am assured,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: I feel such sharp dissension in my breast,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Such fierce alarums both of hope and fear,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: As I am sick with working of my thoughts.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Take therefore shipping; post, my lord, to France;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Agree to any covenants, and procure

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: That Lady Margaret do vouchsafe to come

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: To cross the seas to England and be crown’d

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: King Henry’s faithful and anointed queen.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: For your expenses and sufficient charge,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Among the people gather up a tenth.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Be gone, I say; for till you do return,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: I rest perplexed with a thousand cares.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And you, good uncle, banish all offence.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: If you do censure me by what you were,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Not what you are, I know it will excuse

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: This sudden execution of my will.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And so conduct me where, from company,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: I may revolve and ruminate my grief.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: GLOUCESTER
lines.text: Ay, grief, I fear me, both at first and last.
[_Exeunt Gloucester and Exeter._]

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Thus Suffolk hath prevail’d; and thus he goes,

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: As did the youthful Paris once to Greece,

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: With hope to find the like event in love,

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: But prosper better than the Troyan did.

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: Margaret shall now be queen, and rule the King;

lines.speaker: SUFFOLK
lines.text: But I will rule both her, the King, and realm.
[_Exit._]
